quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The jinn said, 'It guides to the truth and to a straight path (ṭarīqin mustaqīm)' (46:30). 'We have created above you seven paths (ṭarā'iq)' (23:17). 'By the sky and the night-comer (al-ṭāriq)' — 'the piercing star' (86:1–3).

primaryMeaning: Al-Ṭūr is a mountain — above all Mount Sinai, where Allah spoke to Musa. Ṭawr is also a stage or phase.
extendedMeaning: 'He created you in stages (aṭwārā)' (71:14). Surah 52 is Al-Ṭūr, 'the Mount' (52:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'We raised above you the Mount (al-ṭūr)' (2:63). Musa was called 'from the right side of the Mount (al-ṭūr)' (19:52). 'By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai (ṭūri sīnīn)' (95:2).

primaryMeaning: Grapes. ʿInab is grapes; aʿnāb are grapevines.
extendedMeaning: The deniers demanded 'a garden of palms and grapes (ʿinabin)' as a sign (17:91).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times, among Allah's blessings: 'gardens of grapevines (aʿnābin)' (6:99), and 'from the fruits of the palm and the grapes (al-aʿnāb) you take intoxicant and good provision' (16:67). He causes to grow 'olives, palms and grapes (al-aʿnāb)' (16:11).

primaryMeaning: To cover over something completely. Ghamām are clouds that cover the sky; ghamm is grief that covers the heart; ghumma is something covered and unclear.
extendedMeaning: Yunus was saved 'from the distress (al-ghamm)' (21:88). 'Do they wait for Allah to come to them in shadows of clouds (al-ghamām)?' (2:210).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'We shaded you with clouds (al-ghamām)' (2:57). At Uhud 'He repaid you with distress upon distress (ghamman bi-ghammin)', then 'sent down on you, after the distress, security' (3:153–154). 'Let not your affair be in obscurity (ghummatan) to you' (10:71).

primaryMeaning: Rage — intense anger boiling inside. Ghayẓ is fury; ghāẓa is to enrage.
extendedMeaning: Hell 'almost bursts with rage (min al-ghayẓ)' (67:8). They will hear its 'raging (taghayyuẓan) and roaring' (25:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The God-conscious are those 'who restrain anger (al-ghayẓ) and pardon people' (3:134). 'Die in your rage (bi-ghayẓikum)' (3:119). The believers are like a crop 'that the sowers admire, so that He may enrage (li-yaghīẓa) the disbelievers through them' (48:29).

primaryMeaning: A group or company of people — especially a band gathered to fight. Fi'a is a company; fi'atān are two groups.
extendedMeaning: 'What is the matter with you that you are two groups (fi'atayn) concerning the hypocrites?' (4:88). 'Your forces (fi'atukum) will not avail you at all' (8:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'How many a small company (fi'atin) has overcome a large company by Allah's permission' (2:249). 'There was a sign for you in the two hosts (fi'atayn) that met' — at Badr (3:13). 'When you meet a company (fi'atan), stand firm' (8:45).

primaryMeaning: To flee, to run away from something. Firār is flight; mafarr is a place of escape.
extendedMeaning: 'Man will say that Day, "Where is the escape (al-mafarr)?"' (75:10). 'So flee (fa-firrū) to Allah' (51:50).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'The Day a man will flee (yafirru) from his brother, his mother and his father' (80:34–35). 'The death from which you flee (tafirrūna) will meet you' (62:8). 'Flight (al-firār) will not benefit you if you flee from death' (33:16).

primaryMeaning: To limit and fall short. Qaṣura is to be short; qaṣara is to shorten or confine; qaṣr is a palace — a confined, enclosed dwelling; qāṣirāt al-ṭarf are those who limit their glances.
extendedMeaning: Pilgrims enter 'with heads shaved or hair shortened (muqaṣṣirīn)' (48:27). Their brothers the devils 'do not fall short (lā yuqṣirūn)' in leading them astray (7:202).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'There is no blame on you if you shorten (taqṣurū) the prayer' when travelling in fear (4:101). The companions of Paradise are 'limiting their glances (qāṣirāt al-ṭarf)' (37:48). Thamud 'took palaces (quṣūran) in its plains' (7:74).

primaryMeaning: Words with no worth or meaning — idle, empty talk. Laghw is vain speech; laghw in oaths is what is said without intention.
extendedMeaning: The deniers said, 'Do not listen to this Quran, and make noise (wal-ghaw) during it' (41:26).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The believers are 'those who turn away from idle talk (al-laghw)' (23:3). 'Allah will not hold you to account for thoughtless (bil-laghw) oaths' (2:225). In Paradise 'they will hear no idle talk (laghwan) there, only peace' (19:62).

primaryMeaning: To come down to water — to arrive at a watering place. Warada is to arrive; wārid is the one sent to draw water; wird is a herd arriving to drink; warda is a rose, red like a flower.
extendedMeaning: When Musa 'arrived at (warada) the water of Madyan' (28:23). 'When the sky is split and becomes rose-red (wardatan)' (55:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. A caravan 'sent their water-drawer (wāridahum)' and found Yusuf (12:19). 'There is none of you but will pass over it (wāriduhā)' (19:71). 'We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty (wirdan)' (19:86).

primaryMeaning: To light a fire, to make it burn. Waqūd is fuel; awqada is to kindle; mūqad is lit.
extendedMeaning: 'He who made for you fire from the green tree, from which you kindle (tūqidūna)' (36:80). The people of the trench had 'fire full of fuel (al-waqūd)' (85:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'Fear the Fire whose fuel (waqūduhā) is people and stones' (2:24). The deniers 'are the fuel (waqūd) of the Fire' (3:10). The lamp 'is lit (yūqadu) from a blessed olive tree' (24:35).

primaryMeaning: To lean on something for support. Ittaka'a is to recline; muttaka' is a cushion or a place to recline; tawakka'a is to lean on a staff.
extendedMeaning: The wife of al-ʿAzīz 'prepared for them a banquet (muttaka'an)' — a place to recline (12:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times, mostly for the people of Paradise 'reclining (muttaki'īna) therein on adorned couches' (18:31), and 'they and their spouses in shade, reclining (muttaki'ūna) on couches' (36:56). Musa said of his staff, 'I lean (atawakka'u) on it' (20:18).

primaryMeaning: To head for something with intent, to aim at it. Tayammama is to seek out — used for purifying with clean earth when water cannot be found; yamm is the sea.
extendedMeaning: Musa's mother was told, 'cast him into the river (al-yamm)' (20:39; 28:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'If you find no water, then seek (fa-tayammamū) clean earth' (4:43; 5:6). 'Do not aim (lā tayammamū) at the bad of it to spend' (2:267). Pharaoh's people were drowned 'in the sea (al-yamm)' (7:136).

primaryMeaning: The root, the base on which a thing rests. Aṣl is a root or origin; aṣīl is the late afternoon — the base of the day.
extendedMeaning: 'Glorify Him morning and late afternoon (aṣīlan)' (33:42). 'Remember your Lord … in the mornings and the evenings (al-āṣāl)' (7:205).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'A good tree, whose root (aṣluhā) is firm and whose branches are in the sky' (14:24). The tree of Zaqqūm 'comes out of the bottom (aṣl) of Hellfire' (37:64). Palm trees left 'standing on their roots (uṣūlihā)' (59:5).

primaryMeaning: To seize with violence and force. Baṭsh is a violent grip; baṭasha is to strike hard.
extendedMeaning: 'We destroyed those stronger than them in power (baṭshan)' (43:8). Musa was about to 'strike (yabṭisha) the one who was an enemy to both of them' (28:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'The seizure (baṭsh) of your Lord is severe' (85:12). 'The Day We will seize with the greatest seizure (al-baṭshata al-kubrā)' (44:16). Hud told ʿĀd, 'When you seize (baṭashtum), you seize as tyrants' (26:130).

primaryMeaning: To set a broken bone — to mend by force — and so to compel. Jabbār is one who compels others to his will — a tyrant when said of people; al-Jabbār is the Compeller, who also mends what is broken.
extendedMeaning: 'You are not one to compel (bi-jabbārin) them' (50:45). The spies said, 'In it are a people of tyrannical strength (jabbārīn)' (5:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Al-Jabbār is a name of Allah (59:23). Of people, it is blame: ʿĀd 'followed the command of every stubborn tyrant (jabbārin)' (11:59). Yahya was 'not a tyrant (jabbāran), disobedient' (19:14).

primaryMeaning: To cut; and to be new — a garment freshly cut from the loom. Jadīd is new; judad are streaks or tracts; jadd is majesty and greatness.
extendedMeaning: Among the mountains are 'streaks (judadun), white and red' (35:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, mostly in the deniers' doubt about resurrection: 'When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation (khalqin jadīd)?' (13:5), and 'will we be raised as a new creation (jadīdā)?' (17:49). 'Exalted is the majesty (jaddu) of our Lord' (72:3).

primaryMeaning: To close in on someone from every side and befall them — used only for evil that recoils on those who caused it.
extendedMeaning: 'The evil plot encloses (yaḥīqu) none but its own people' (35:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, mostly in 'what they used to mock surrounded them (ḥāqa)': 'those who mocked were surrounded (fa-ḥāqa) by what they used to ridicule' (6:10), and 'what they used to mock will surround them (ḥāqa)' (11:8).

primaryMeaning: To push away, to drive back — and to hand over. Dafaʿa is to repel or deliver; dāfiʿ is one who wards off.
extendedMeaning: Orphans' property is to be 'delivered (fa-dfaʿū) to them' when they come of age (4:6). The punishment has 'no preventer (dāfiʿ)' (70:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'Repel (idfaʿ) evil with what is better' (23:96; 41:34). 'Were it not for Allah repelling (dafʿu) some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted' (2:251). 'Allah defends (yudāfiʿu) those who believe' (22:38).

primaryMeaning: To destroy completely, to wipe out. Dammara is to annihilate; tadmīr is utter destruction.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah destroyed (dammara) them, and for the disbelievers is the like' (47:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, for the destruction of earlier peoples: 'then We destroyed them (dammarnāhum) with utter destruction' (25:36), and 'We destroyed (dammarnā) what Pharaoh and his people were making' (7:137). ʿĀd's wind was 'destroying (tudammiru) everything by the command of its Lord' (46:25).

primaryMeaning: Blood. Dam is blood; dimā' is its plural — used both literally and for shedding blood, killing.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf's brothers brought his shirt 'with false blood (bi-damin kadhib)' (12:18). 'Their meat and their blood (dimā'uhā) do not reach Allah' (22:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'He has forbidden you carrion, blood (al-dam) and the flesh of swine' (2:173). The angels asked, 'Will You place in it one who will cause corruption and shed blood (al-dimā')?' (2:30). 'Do not shed your blood (dimā'akum)' (2:84).

primaryMeaning: Something that shakes and disturbs — a trembling that comes with sickness. Rijz is a punishment that strikes and shakes, and also filth and uncleanness.
extendedMeaning: 'And uncleanliness (al-rujz), avoid' (74:5). Rain was sent down to 'remove from you the evil (rijz) of Satan' (8:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'We sent down upon the wrongdoers a punishment (rijzan) from the sky' (2:59). Pharaoh's people begged Musa, 'If you remove the punishment (al-rijz) from us, we will believe' (7:134). 'For them is a punishment of painful foulness (rijzin alīm)' (34:5).

primaryMeaning: Filth — something unclean and repugnant, physical or moral. Rijs is an abomination.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah only intends to remove impurity (al-rijs) from you, people of the house' (33:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'Wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination (rijsun) from the work of Satan' (5:90). 'Thus Allah places filth (al-rijs) on those who do not believe' (6:125). 'Avoid the filth (al-rijs) of idols' (22:30).

primaryMeaning: To tend and look after, as a shepherd keeps his flock. Raʿā is to pasture or guard; rāʿī is a shepherd or keeper; marʿā is pasture; riʿāya is care and observance.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not say rāʿinā but say unẓurnā' (2:104) — a word some twisted into an insult. Shuʿayb's daughters waited 'until the shepherds (al-riʿā') leave' (28:23).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. The believers are 'those who keep (rāʿūn) their trusts and their promises' (23:8). 'He brought out from it its water and its pasture (marʿāhā)' (79:31). The monks' invented monasticism: 'they did not observe it (raʿawhā) with due observance' (57:27).

primaryMeaning: To come over someone and cover them — to overtake, to burden. Rahiqa is to cover; arhaqa is to overburden; rahaq is burden and distress.
extendedMeaning: Some men sought refuge in jinn, 'but they only increased them in burden (rahaqan)' (72:6). Musa asked, 'Do not be hard on me (turhiqnī)' (18:73).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'Neither darkness nor humiliation will cover (yarhaqu) their faces' — the people of Paradise (10:26), while 'humiliation will cover them (tarhaquhum)' — the deniers (68:43). The boy would have 'burdened them (yurhiqahumā) with transgression and disbelief' (18:80).

primaryMeaning: To come near, to advance close. Zulfā is nearness; azlafa is to bring near; zulaf are hours that are near to each other.
extendedMeaning: 'Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in parts (zulafan) of the night' (11:114).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. The idolaters claim, 'We worship them only that they bring us near (zulfā) to Allah' (39:3). 'Paradise will be brought near (uzlifat) to the God-conscious' (26:90). Dawud and Sulayman had 'nearness (la-zulfā) to Us and a good return' (38:25, 38:40).

primaryMeaning: To move away from a place. It is mostly used as mā zāla and lā yazālu, 'did not cease' or 'will not cease' — something continuing. Zayyala is to separate.
extendedMeaning: 'Then We will separate them (fa-zayyalnā)' — the worshippers from what they worshipped (10:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, mostly for things that continue: 'They will not cease (lā yazālūna) fighting you until they turn you back from your religion' (2:217). 'They will not cease (lā yazālūna) to differ' (11:118). 'Their building will not cease (lā yazālu) to be a doubt in their hearts' (9:110).

primaryMeaning: To be low, the lowest point — the opposite of ʿuluww, 'height'. Asfal is lowest; sāfil is the lower side.
extendedMeaning: 'We created man in the best stature, then returned him to the lowest of the low (asfala sāfilīn)' (95:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'We made its highest part its lowest (sāfilahā)' — the cities of Lut (11:82). 'The hypocrites will be in the lowest (al-asfal) depth of the Fire' (4:145). 'He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest (al-suflā)' (9:40).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: blackness, the opposite of whiteness, and leadership — sayyid is a master or chief, one who stands out.
extendedMeaning: The wife of al-ʿAzīz and Yusuf 'found her husband (sayyidahā) at the door' (12:25). The fast ends 'when the white thread becomes distinct from the black (al-aswad) thread' (2:187).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'The Day some faces will turn white and some faces black (taswaddu)' (3:106). When told of a daughter, 'his face becomes dark (muswaddan)' (16:58). Yahya was 'a leader (sayyidan), chaste, and a prophet' (3:39).

primaryMeaning: To laugh — from a smile to open laughter. Aḍḥaka is to make laugh.
extendedMeaning: 'The criminals used to laugh (yaḍḥakūna) at those who believed', and on that Day 'the believers will laugh at the disbelievers' (83:29, 83:34). Faces 'laughing (ḍāḥikatun), rejoicing' (80:39).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'It is He who makes laugh (aḍḥaka) and makes weep' (53:43). Sarah 'laughed (fa-ḍaḥikat)' at the news of a son (11:71). Sulayman 'smiled, laughing (ḍāḥikan) at her words' — the ant (27:19).

primaryMeaning: To be lost and wasted. Aḍāʿa is to let something go to waste or to neglect it.
extendedMeaning: 'After them came successors who neglected (aḍāʿū) prayer and followed desires' (19:59).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, mostly in 'Allah does not let go to waste (lā yuḍīʿu) the reward of the believers' (3:171), and 'I do not let go to waste (lā uḍīʿu) the work of any of you, male or female' (3:195). 'Allah would never let your faith go to waste (li-yuḍīʿa)' (2:143).

primaryMeaning: To be long, to stretch out in length or time. Ṭūl is length; ṭawīl is long; ṭawl is abundance and means — having enough to reach something.
extendedMeaning: Allah is 'Owner of abundance (dhī al-ṭawl)' (40:3). Whoever lacks 'the means (ṭawlan)' to marry a free believing woman (4:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'You will never reach the mountains in height (ṭūlan)' (17:37). 'Has the time not come … lest their hearts be like those given the Book before, and the time was prolonged (fa-ṭāla) for them, so their hearts hardened?' (57:16). 'Glorify Him through a long (ṭawīlan) night' (76:26).

primaryMeaning: To rise in arrogance and exceed every limit — insolent defiance. ʿUtuww is insolence; ʿatā is to rebel; ʿitiyy is extreme old age, going beyond the usual span.
extendedMeaning: Zakariyya said, 'I have reached extreme (ʿitiyyā) old age' (19:8). 'How many a town rebelled (ʿatat) against the command of its Lord' (65:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Thamud 'were insolent (ʿataw) towards the command of their Lord' (7:77). 'They were insolent (ʿataw) with great insolence (ʿutuwwan)' (25:21). ʿĀd were destroyed 'by a violent (ʿātiya) wind' (69:6).

primaryMeaning: To set aside, to separate from others. Iʿtazala is to withdraw, to keep apart; maʿzil is a place apart.
extendedMeaning: 'Keep away from (fa-ʿtazilū) wives during menstruation' (2:222). Musa said, 'If you do not believe me, leave me alone (fa-ʿtazilūni)' (44:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Ibrahim said, 'I will leave you (aʿtazilukum) and what you invoke' (19:48). The youths said, 'When you have withdrawn from them (iʿtazaltumūhum), take refuge in the cave' (18:16). Nuh's son 'was apart (fī maʿzil)' (11:42).

primaryMeaning: To be pure and holy — free of every impurity. Quds is holiness; muqaddas is sanctified; al-Quddūs is the Most Holy; qaddasa is to declare holy.
extendedMeaning: Musa was 'in the sacred valley (al-muqaddas), Ṭuwā' (20:12). 'Enter the holy land (al-arḍ al-muqaddasa)' (5:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Rūḥ al-qudus, 'the Holy Spirit' — Jibrīl — supported ʿĪsā (2:87). The angels said, 'We glorify You with praise and sanctify (nuqaddisu) You' (2:30). Al-Quddūs, 'the Holy One', is a name of Allah (59:23).

primaryMeaning: To overpower, to prevail over someone completely. Qahr is subjugation; al-Qāhir and al-Qahhār are the Subduer, the Irresistible.
extendedMeaning: 'As for the orphan, do not oppress (taqhar) him' (93:9). Pharaoh said, 'we are subjugators (qāhirūn) over them' (7:127).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'He is the Subjugator (al-qāhir) over His servants' (6:18). Yusuf asked, 'Are many lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible (al-qahhār)?' (12:39). On the Day of Judgment all come forth 'to Allah, the One, the Irresistible' (14:48).

primaryMeaning: To take charge of someone and provide for them — to stand as guarantor. Kafala is to take care of; kafīl is a guarantor; kifl is a share or portion.
extendedMeaning: Dhū al-Kifl is named among the patient (21:85). 'He will give you a double portion (kiflayn) of His mercy' (57:28). 'You have made Allah a guarantor (kafīlan) over you' (16:91).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Zakariyya 'was put in charge (kaffalahā)' of Maryam (3:37), after they cast lots over 'which of them should take charge (yakfulu) of Maryam' (3:44). Musa's sister asked, 'Shall I show you someone who will nurse and rear him (yakfuluhu)?' (20:40).

primaryMeaning: A hundred. Mi'a is a hundred; mi'atān is two hundred.
extendedMeaning: The people of the Cave stayed 'three hundred (mi'atin) years' (18:25). Yunus was sent 'to a hundred thousand (mi'ati alfin) or more' (37:147).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. Allah caused a man 'to die for a hundred (mi'ata) years, then raised him' (2:259). 'Twenty patient ones will overcome two hundred (mi'atayn)' (8:65). 'In each spike a hundred (mi'atu) grains' (2:261).

primaryMeaning: A stretch of time — to extend it and give more. Amlā is to grant respite, to let someone go on for a time; malī is a long while; amlā is also to dictate.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim's father said, 'Leave me for a long while (maliyyan)' (19:46). 'They are dictated (tumlā) to him morning and evening' — the deniers' claim about the Quran (25:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times, mostly for Allah granting respite: 'Let not the disbelievers think that We give them respite (numlī) for their good; We give them respite only so they increase in sin' (3:178). 'I give them respite (umlī); My plan is firm' (7:183). 'I granted respite (amlaytu) to the disbelievers, then seized them' (13:32).

primaryMeaning: To become less, to fall short. Naqaṣa is to decrease; naqṣ is loss.
extendedMeaning: 'We know what the earth diminishes (tanquṣu) of them' — the bodies of the dead (50:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 10 times. 'We will test you with something of fear, hunger and loss (naqṣin) of wealth, lives and fruits' (2:155). Shuʿayb said, 'Do not decrease (lā tanquṣū) the measure and weight' (11:84). 'We come to the land, reducing it (nanquṣuhā) from its borders' (13:41).

primaryMeaning: To scatter, to spread about. Baththa is to disperse; mabthūth is scattered; bathth is grief poured out, spread from the heart.
extendedMeaning: Yaʿqub said, 'I only complain of my suffering (baththī) and my grief to Allah' (12:86). The mountains become 'dust dispersing (munbaththā)' (56:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'He spread (baththa) from them many men and women' (4:1). Rain revives the earth 'and He dispersed (baththa) in it every kind of creature' (2:164). On the Last Day people will be 'like scattered (al-mabthūth) moths' (101:4).

primaryMeaning: To come out into the open, to appear plainly. Baraza is to emerge; burriza is to be brought into view.
extendedMeaning: 'When they went forth (barazū) to face Jalut and his soldiers' (2:250). 'The Day they come out (bārizūn), nothing about them is hidden from Allah' (40:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. On the Day of Judgment 'they will come forth (barazū) to Allah all together' (14:21). 'The Hellfire will be brought into view (burrizat) for the deviators' (26:91). 'You will see the earth laid bare (bārizatan)' (18:47).

primaryMeaning: Cattle — the cow. Classically linked to baqara, 'to split open', as cattle split the soil in ploughing.
extendedMeaning: Some cattle and sheep fat was forbidden to the Jews (6:146).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times, mostly in the story that gives Surah 2 its name: 'Allah commands you to slaughter a cow (baqaratan)' (2:67), 'a yellow cow, bright in colour' (2:69). The king saw 'seven fat cows (baqarātin) eaten by seven lean ones' (12:43).

primaryMeaning: Trade — buying and selling for profit. Tijāra is commerce or a transaction.
extendedMeaning: 'When they saw trade (tijāratan) or amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing' (62:11). Believers 'hope for a trade that will never perish' (35:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Their trade (tijāratuhum) did not profit' — those who bought error for guidance (2:16). Men 'whom neither trade (tijāratun) nor sale distracts from remembering Allah' (24:37). 'Shall I guide you to a trade (tijāratin) that will save you from a painful punishment?' (61:10).

primaryMeaning: To burn with fire. Ḥarīq is burning; ḥarraqa is to burn up.
extendedMeaning: A garden struck by 'a whirlwind with fire, and it is burnt (fa-ḥtaraqat)' (2:266).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Taste the punishment of the burning (al-ḥarīq)' (3:181). Ibrahim's people said, 'Burn him (ḥarriqūhu) and support your gods' (21:68). Musa told the Samiri, 'We will surely burn it (la-nuḥarriqannahu)' — the calf (20:97).

primaryMeaning: Adornment, jewellery. Ḥilya is an ornament; ḥullā is to be adorned.
extendedMeaning: 'Is one brought up among ornaments (al-ḥilya) and unclear in argument …?' (43:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. In Paradise 'they will be adorned (yuḥallawna) with bracelets of gold' (18:31). From the sea 'you bring out ornaments (ḥilyatan) to wear' (16:14). The Israelites made a calf 'from their ornaments (ḥuliyyihim)' (7:148).

primaryMeaning: To imagine, to picture something — and pride, being taken with one's own image. Khuyyila is to seem; mukhtāl is conceited; khayl, 'horses', are classically linked to their proud bearing.
extendedMeaning: Horses (al-khayl) are among the things made attractive (3:14), created 'for you to ride and as adornment' (16:8). 'Prepare against them … war horses (al-khayl)' (8:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Allah does not love every conceited (mukhtālin), boastful one' (31:18). Musa saw their ropes: 'it seemed to him (yukhayyalu) from their magic that they were moving' (20:66).

primaryMeaning: To last and continue without stopping. Dāma is to endure; dā'im is lasting; mā dāma is 'as long as'.
extendedMeaning: They abide 'as long as the heavens and the earth endure (mā dāmati)' (11:107). He enjoined on ʿĪsā 'prayer and zakah as long as I live (mā dumtu ḥayyā)' (19:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. Its food 'is lasting (dā'imun), and its shade' — Paradise (13:35). 'Those who are constant (dā'imūn) in their prayer' (70:23). ʿĪsā said, 'I was a witness over them as long as I remained (mā dumtu) among them' (5:117).

primaryMeaning: To slaughter by cutting the throat. Dhabaḥa is to slaughter; dhibḥ is a sacrifice.
extendedMeaning: Forbidden is 'what was sacrificed (dhubiḥa) on stone altars' (5:3). Sulayman said of the hoopoe, 'I will surely slaughter it' (27:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. Pharaoh's people were 'slaughtering (yudhabbiḥūna) your sons' (2:49). 'Allah commands you to slaughter (tadhbaḥū) a cow' (2:67). Ibrahim said, 'I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you (adhbaḥuka)' (37:102), and 'We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (bi-dhibḥin)' (37:107).

primaryMeaning: To throw, to shoot. Ramā is to cast; it also means to accuse — to throw a charge at someone.
extendedMeaning: 'It throws (tarmī) sparks as huge as castles' — Hell (77:32). 'Whoever earns a fault or sin, then throws it (yarmi) on an innocent' (4:112).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'You did not throw (ramayta) when you threw, but it was Allah who threw' (8:17). Those who accuse (yarmūna) chaste women without four witnesses are flogged (24:4). Birds were 'striking them (tarmīhim) with stones of baked clay' (105:4).

primaryMeaning: Unlawful sexual intercourse. Zinā is fornication or adultery; zānin and zāniya are the man and woman who commit it.
extendedMeaning: The believing women pledged 'not to steal and not to commit adultery (yaznīna)' (60:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse (al-zinā); it is an immorality and an evil way' (17:32). Its punishment is set in 24:2. The servants of the Most Merciful 'do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse (yaznūn)' (25:68).

primaryMeaning: To swerve, to turn aside from what is straight. Zāgha is to deviate; zaygh is perversity; azāgha is to cause to deviate.
extendedMeaning: 'The sight did not swerve (mā zāgha), nor did it transgress' (53:17). At the trench 'eyes grew wild (zāghat)' (33:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'As for those in whose hearts is deviation (zayghun), they follow what is unclear' (3:7). 'Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate (lā tuzigh) after You have guided us' (3:8). 'When they deviated (zāghū), Allah caused their hearts to deviate (azāgha)' (61:5).

primaryMeaning: To cut off and rest — to stop work. Sabt is the Sabbath, the day of rest; subāt is rest, a break from activity.
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'You knew those among you who transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath (al-sabt)' (2:65). Their fish came to them 'on the day of their Sabbath (sabtihim)' (7:163). 'The Sabbath was made only for those who differed over it' (16:124).

primaryMeaning: To steal — to take something secretly. Saraqa is to steal; sāriq is a thief; istaraqa is to steal a hearing — to eavesdrop.
extendedMeaning: The devils are guarded from heaven 'except one who steals a hearing (istaraqa)' (15:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'As for the male thief (al-sāriq) and the female thief, cut off their hands' (5:38). A crier called out to Yusuf's brothers, 'You are thieves (la-sāriqūn)' (12:70). The believing women pledged 'not to steal (lā yasriqna)' (60:12).

primaryMeaning: Something flat and wide — a sheet or page. Ṣaḥīfa is a written page; ṣuḥuf are scriptures; ṣiḥāf are broad plates.
extendedMeaning: In Paradise 'plates (bi-ṣiḥāfin) of gold will be passed among them' (43:71).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'This is in the former scriptures (al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā), the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa' (87:18–19). The Quran is 'in honoured sheets (ṣuḥufin mukarrama)' (80:13). 'When the pages (al-ṣuḥuf) are spread open' (81:10).

primaryMeaning: To go up, to climb. Ṣaʿida is to ascend; ṣaʿīd is the face of the earth — the upper surface; ṣaʿad is a hard climb, a severe punishment.
extendedMeaning: 'I will cover him with a laborious climb (ṣaʿūdā)' (74:17). At Uhud, 'you were running uphill (tuṣʿidūna) without looking back' (3:153).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'To Him ascends (yaṣʿadu) the good word' (35:10). The breast of the one left astray is tight 'as though he were climbing (yaṣṣaʿʿadu) into the sky' (6:125). Without water, 'seek clean earth (ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban)' (4:43).

primaryMeaning: To cross over from one side to another. ʿAbara is to pass through; ʿibra is a lesson — crossing from what is seen to what it teaches; ʿabbara is to interpret dreams.
extendedMeaning: The king asked, 'Explain to me my dream, if you can interpret (taʿburūn) dreams' (12:43). The rules of prayer allow 'one passing through (ʿābirī sabīl)' (4:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'In their stories is a lesson (ʿibratun) for people of understanding' (12:111). 'In that is a lesson (la-ʿibratan) for those who have eyes' (3:13). 'Take a lesson (fa-ʿtabirū), O you who have sight' (59:2).

primaryMeaning: To go up by stages; and to limp. ʿAraja is to ascend; maʿārij are the ways of ascent; aʿraj is lame.
extendedMeaning: Allah is 'Owner of the ways of ascent (dhī al-maʿārij)' (70:3). 'There is no blame on the lame (al-aʿraj)' (24:61).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it, what comes down from the sky and what ascends (yaʿruju) into it' (57:4). 'The angels and the Spirit ascend (taʿruju) to Him in a Day whose length is fifty thousand years' (70:4).

primaryMeaning: Firm resolve — making up one's mind and holding to it. ʿAzm is determination; ʿazama is to resolve.
extendedMeaning: 'Be patient as were those of determination (ulū al-ʿazm) among the messengers' (46:35).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'That is of the matters of determination (ʿazm al-umūr)' — patience and piety (3:186; 31:17). 'When you have decided (ʿazamta), rely on Allah' (3:159). Of Adam: 'We found in him no firm resolve (ʿazman)' (20:115).

primaryMeaning: To stay close to something and devote oneself to it. ʿAkafa is to remain in devotion; ʿākif is one who stays — in a mosque for worship, or by an idol.
extendedMeaning: Musa said to the Samiri, 'Look at your god to which you remained devoted (ʿākifan)' (20:97). The offering was 'prevented (maʿkūfan) from reaching its place' (48:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Do not approach them while you are in retreat (ʿākifūn) in the mosques' (2:187). Ibrahim asked, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted (ʿākifūn)?' (21:52). The House is purified 'for those who seclude themselves (al-ʿākifīn)' (2:125).

primaryMeaning: The neck. ʿUnuq is a neck; aʿnāq are necks.
extendedMeaning: 'Strike above the necks (al-aʿnāq)' — at Badr (8:12). 'Their necks (aʿnāquhum) would remain humbled to it' — a sign from the sky (26:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Those will have shackles on their necks (aʿnāqihim)' (13:5). 'Every person's fate We have fastened to his neck (ʿunuqihi)' (17:13). 'Do not make your hand chained to your neck (ʿunuqika)' (17:29).

primaryMeaning: To bend, to be crooked. ʿIwaj is crookedness — in something abstract such as religion or speech, as opposed to physical bending.
extendedMeaning: On that Day they follow the caller 'with no deviation (ʿiwaja) in it' (20:108).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'All praise is for Allah, who sent down the Book to His servant and placed in it no crookedness (ʿiwajā)' (18:1). The deniers 'seek to make it crooked (ʿiwajan)' — the way of Allah (3:99). 'An Arabic Quran without any deviance (ʿiwajin)' (39:28).

primaryMeaning: A year. ʿĀm is a year — a full cycle of the seasons.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf foretold 'a year (ʿāmun) in which people will be given rain' (12:49). The polytheists must not approach the Sacred Mosque 'after this, their final year (ʿāmihim)' (9:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. Allah caused a man 'to die for a hundred years (ʿāmin)' (2:259). Nuh remained among his people 'a thousand years less fifty years (ʿāman)' (29:14). Weaning is 'in two years (ʿāmayn)' (31:14).

primaryMeaning: To gain something without hardship. Ghanam are sheep; ghanīma and maghānim are spoils — what is gained in war.
extendedMeaning: Dawud and Sulayman judged 'the field into which the people's sheep (ghanamu) strayed at night' (21:78).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Know that whatever you obtain as spoils (ghanimtum), one-fifth is for Allah and the Messenger' (8:41). 'Allah promised you much spoils (maghānim) that you will take' (48:20). Musa said of his staff, 'I beat leaves with it for my sheep (ghanamī)' (20:18).

primaryMeaning: A gap, an opening between two things. Farj is an opening — used for the private parts, and so for chastity; furūj are rifts; furijat is to be split open.
extendedMeaning: 'Have they not looked at the sky … it has no rifts (furūj)' (50:6). 'When the sky is split open (furijat)' (77:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times, mostly for chastity: the believers 'guard their private parts (furūjihim)' (23:5), and 'tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts (furūjahum)' (24:30). Maryam 'guarded her chastity (farjahā)' (21:91; 66:12).

primaryMeaning: To break apart and scatter. Infaḍḍa is to disperse. Fiḍḍa, 'silver', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: 'Vessels of silver (fiḍḍatin) and cups of crystal' in Paradise (76:15). The hypocrites said, 'Do not spend on those with the Messenger until they disband (yanfaḍḍū)' (63:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Had you been harsh, they would have dispersed (la-nfaḍḍū) from around you' (3:159). 'When they saw trade or amusement, they rushed (infaḍḍū) to it' (62:11). 'Those who hoard gold and silver (al-fiḍḍa)' face a painful punishment (9:34).

primaryMeaning: To overflow, to pour out abundantly. Fāḍa is to flow over; afāḍa is to pour out — and to move on in a great stream, as the pilgrims do.
extendedMeaning: 'He knows best what you are engaged (tufīḍūna) in' (46:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'You see their eyes overflowing (tafīḍu) with tears' at the truth (5:83). 'When you depart (afaḍtum) from ʿArafāt, remember Allah' (2:198), and 'depart from where the people depart' (2:199). The people of the Fire call, 'Pour (afīḍū) on us some water' (7:50).

primaryMeaning: To grasp, to close the hand on something. Qabaḍa is to take hold of, and to withhold; qabḍa is a handful or grip.
extendedMeaning: The Samiri said, 'I took a handful (qabḍatan) from the track of the messenger' (20:96). Birds 'spreading and folding (yaqbiḍna) their wings' (67:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Allah withholds (yaqbiḍu) and extends' (2:245). 'The whole earth will be in His grip (qabḍatuhu) on the Day of Resurrection' (39:67). The hypocrites 'close (yaqbiḍūna) their hands' — withholding charity (9:67).

primaryMeaning: To throw or hurl with force, over a distance. Qadhafa is to cast; it is also used for casting fear into hearts.
extendedMeaning: The devils 'are pelted (yuqdhafūna) from every side' (37:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'He cast (qadhafa) terror into their hearts' (33:26; 59:2). 'We hurl (naqdhifu) the truth against falsehood and it destroys it' (21:18). Musa's mother was told, 'Cast him (iqdhifīhi) into the chest, then cast it into the river' (20:39).

primaryMeaning: To gather and store up — to pack something away. Kanz is a buried treasure; kanaza is to hoard.
extendedMeaning: 'We gave Qarun of treasures (al-kunūz) whose keys would burden a band of strong men' (28:76).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Those who hoard (yaknizūna) gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them news of a painful punishment' (9:34). 'This is what you hoarded (kanaztum) for yourselves' (9:35). Beneath the wall 'was a treasure (kanzun) for them' — the two orphans (18:82).

primaryMeaning: Colour — and by extension a kind or variety. Lawn is colour; alwān are colours or varieties.
extendedMeaning: From bees 'comes a drink of varied colours (alwānuhu), in which is healing' (16:69).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Its colour (lawnuhā) is bright; it pleases those who see it' — the yellow cow (2:69). 'The diversity of your languages and colours (alwānikum)' is a sign (30:22). 'Fruits of varied colours (alwānuhā)' and mountains of varied colours (35:27).

primaryMeaning: To undo what was tied or built — to untwist a rope, to pull down a structure. Naqḍ is breaking a covenant; anqaḍa is to weigh so heavily as to crack.
extendedMeaning: 'Which weighed upon (anqaḍa) your back' — the burden removed from the Prophet (94:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times, mostly for breaking pledges: 'those who break (yanquḍūna) the covenant of Allah after its confirmation' (2:27). 'Do not break (lā tanquḍū) oaths after their confirmation' (16:91), and do not be 'like her who untwisted (naqaḍat) her spun yarn after it was strong' (16:92).

primaryMeaning: Sleep. Nawm is sleep; manām is sleep or the place and time of sleep — and a dream; nā'im is one asleep.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim said, 'I see in a dream (al-manām) that I am sacrificing you' (37:102). Allah showed the Prophet the enemy as few 'in your dream (manāmika)' (8:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Neither drowsiness nor sleep (nawmun) overtakes Him' (2:255). 'Among His signs is your sleep (manāmukum) by night and day' (30:23). 'Allah takes the souls at death, and those that do not die in their sleep (manāmihā)' (39:42).

primaryMeaning: To set one's mind on something, to intend it — and the concern that fills the mind. Hamma bi- is to intend or resolve; ahamma is to cause worry.
extendedMeaning: 'They had determined (hammū) to expel the Messenger' (9:13). At Uhud, 'a group was worried (ahammathum) about themselves' (3:154).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'She certainly determined (hammat) for him, and he would have inclined to her (hamma bihā) had he not seen the proof of his Lord' — Yusuf (12:24). 'Two groups among you were about to lose courage (hammat)' (3:122). 'A people determined (hamma) to stretch their hands against you' (5:11).

primaryMeaning: Heaviness. Waqr is deafness — a weight in the ear; wiqr is a heavy load; waqār is dignified gravity; waqqara is to show respect, to treat as weighty.
extendedMeaning: 'That you may honour him and respect him (tuwaqqirūhu)' (48:9). Nuh asked, 'What is wrong with you that you do not hope for grandeur (waqāran) from Allah?' (71:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'We have placed coverings over their hearts and deafness (waqran) in their ears' (6:25). 'In our ears is deafness (waqrun)' — the deniers (41:5). 'By those carrying a load (wiqran)' — the clouds (51:2).

primaryMeaning: Weakness — in body, bone or resolve. Wahana is to weaken or lose heart; wahn is weakness; awhan is the weakest.
extendedMeaning: Zakariyya said, 'My bones have weakened (wahana)' (19:4). 'The weakest (awhana) of houses is the house of the spider' (29:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 9 times. 'Do not weaken (lā tahinū) and do not grieve' (3:139). 'His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness (wahnan ʿalā wahn)' (31:14). The companions of the prophets 'did not lose heart (fa-mā wahanū)' (3:146).

primaryMeaning: The right time for something — a moment reached, or something fully reached, as boiling water. Ānā' are hours; anā is to come due; ān is extremely hot; āniya is a vessel.
extendedMeaning: 'Vessels (bi-āniyatin) of silver' in Paradise (76:15). 'Do not enter … without waiting for its preparation (ināhu)' — a meal (33:53).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. The upright 'recite the verses of Allah during the hours (ānā') of the night' (3:113). 'Has the time not come (a-lam ya'ni) for those who believe that their hearts humble themselves?' (57:16). The people of the Fire drink 'from a boiling (āniyatin) spring' (88:5).

Occurs 8 times. The Israelites said, 'Now (al-āna) you have come with the truth' (2:71). 'Now (al-āna) Allah has lightened it for you' (8:66). Pharaoh, drowning, declared belief — and was told, 'Now (āl'āna)? And you disobeyed before' (10:91).

primaryMeaning: Burhān is a decisive proof — evidence so clear that it settles the matter.
extendedMeaning: Musa's staff and hand were 'two proofs (burhānān) from your Lord' (28:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Bring your proof (burhānakum), if you are truthful' — asked of those with false claims (2:111). 'O mankind, there has come to you a proof (burhānun) from your Lord' (4:174). Yusuf would have inclined 'had he not seen the proof (burhān) of his Lord' (12:24).

primaryMeaning: To leave someone stunned and speechless. Buhita is to be dumbfounded; buhtān is a slander so false that it stuns the one accused.
extendedMeaning: The Hour 'will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them (fa-tabhatuhum)' (21:40). The women pledged 'not to bring a slander (bi-buhtānin)' (60:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. When Ibrahim challenged the king to bring the sun from the west, 'the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded (fa-buhita)' (2:258). Of the slander against ʿĀ'isha: 'This is a great slander (buhtānun ʿaẓīm)' (24:16).

primaryMeaning: Ease and luxury — a soft life that can lead to excess. Atrafa is to give someone luxury; mutraf is one spoilt by comfort.
extendedMeaning: The companions of the left 'were before that indulging in affluence (mutrafīn)' (56:45).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times, always for the affluent who rejected the prophets: 'We did not send a warner to any town except that its affluent (mutrafūhā) said, "We disbelieve"' (34:34). 'When We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent (mutrafīhā), and they defiantly disobey' (17:16).

primaryMeaning: To screen something off, to prevent it from being seen or reached. Ḥijāb is a screen, veil or barrier; maḥjūb is one kept behind a barrier.
extendedMeaning: 'They will be partitioned (la-maḥjūbūn) from their Lord that Day' (83:15). Maryam 'took a screen (ḥijāban) from them' (19:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Between them is a partition (ḥijābun)' — Paradise and the Fire (7:46). 'When you ask them for something, ask from behind a screen (ḥijābin)' (33:53). Allah speaks to man 'only by revelation or from behind a veil (ḥijābin)' (42:51).

primaryMeaning: To seal — to stamp the end of something so nothing more can enter or leave. Khatm is a seal; khātam is the seal that ends a series; khitām is the final part.
extendedMeaning: The righteous drink 'a pure wine, sealed (makhtūm), whose seal (khitāmuhu) is musk' (83:25–26).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Allah has set a seal (khatama) on their hearts' (2:7). Muhammad is 'the Messenger of Allah and the Seal (khātama) of the prophets' (33:40). 'Today We will seal (nakhtimu) their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us' (36:65).

primaryMeaning: To sink down, to go under. Khasafa is for the earth to swallow something, or for the moon to be eclipsed — its light swallowed.
extendedMeaning: 'Among them were those We caused the earth to swallow (khasafnā)' (29:40).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'We caused the earth to swallow (fa-khasafnā) him and his home' — Qarun (28:81). 'Do you feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you (yakhsifa)?' (67:16). On the Last Day 'the moon is eclipsed (khasafa)' (75:8).

primaryMeaning: Green — the colour of fresh, living plants. Akhḍar is green; khaḍir is green growth.
extendedMeaning: 'From it We bring forth green growth (khaḍiran)' (6:99). The king dreamt of 'seven green (khuḍrin) ears' (12:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'The earth becomes green (mukhḍarratan)' after rain (22:63). 'He made fire for you from the green (al-akhḍar) tree' (36:80). The people of Paradise wear 'green (khuḍran) garments of fine silk' (18:31).

primaryMeaning: Five. Khamsūn is fifty; khumus is a fifth; khāmis is fifth.
extendedMeaning: 'No five (khamsatin) confer but He is the sixth' (58:7). 'Your Lord will reinforce you with five (bi-khamsati) thousand angels' (3:125).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Whatever you take as spoils, one fifth (khumusahu) is for Allah' (8:41). Nuh remained 'a thousand years less fifty (khamsīna)' (29:14). A Day 'whose length is fifty (khamsīna) thousand years' (70:4).

primaryMeaning: The root has two senses: the maternal side of kin — khāl is a maternal uncle, khāla a maternal aunt — and bestowing: khawwala is to grant someone something to take care of.
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. Maternal aunts (khālātukum) are named among those forbidden in marriage (4:23). 'You have left behind what We bestowed on you (khawwalnākum)' (6:94). 'When We bestow on him (khawwalnāhu) a favour from Us, he says, "I was given it because of knowledge"' (39:49).

primaryMeaning: To show the way, to point towards something. Dalla is to guide or direct; dalīl is an indication or guide; dallā is to lead down by deception.
extendedMeaning: 'We made the sun an indication (dalīlan) for it' — the shadow (25:45). Nothing 'showed them (dallahum)' Sulayman's death except the creature eating his staff (34:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Shall I show you (adullukum) a trade that will save you?' (61:10). Satan said, 'Shall I direct you (adulluka) to the tree of eternity?' (20:120), and 'he led them down (fa-dallāhumā) by deception' (7:22).

primaryMeaning: To shake violently, to tremble. Rajfa is an earthquake; rājifa is the quaking — the first blast of the Hour; murjif is one who spreads alarming rumours.
extendedMeaning: The hypocrites and 'those who spread rumours (al-murjifūn) in the city' are warned (33:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'The earthquake (al-rajfa) seized them, and they became lifeless in their home' — Thamud and Madyan (7:78). 'The Day the earth and the mountains will quake (tarjufu)' (73:14). 'The Day the quaking one (al-rājifa) quakes' (79:6).

primaryMeaning: To want something eagerly; with ʿan, to turn away from it in dislike. Raghba is longing; rāghib is one who desires.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim's father asked, 'Do you turn away (a-rāghibun) from my gods?' (19:46). 'We turn in hope (rāghibūn) to Allah' (9:59).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Who would turn away (yarghabu ʿan) from the religion of Ibrahim?' (2:130). The prophets 'called on Us in hope (raghaban) and fear' (21:90). 'To your Lord turn your longing (fa-rghab)' (94:8).

primaryMeaning: Six. Sitta is six; sittūn is sixty.
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times, mostly in 'He created the heavens and the earth in six (sittati) days' (7:54). The expiation for ẓihār includes 'feeding sixty (sittīna) poor people' (58:4).

primaryMeaning: To travel by night. Asrā and sarā are to journey at night; sariyy is a stream that flows along.
extendedMeaning: 'Your Lord has placed a stream (sariyyan) beneath you' — to Maryam (19:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Exalted is He who took His servant by night (asrā)' — the Night Journey (17:1). Lut and Musa were told, 'Travel by night (fa-asri) with My servants' (11:81; 20:77). 'By the night when it passes (yasri)' (89:4).

primaryMeaning: To fall down from a height. Saqaṭa is to fall; asqaṭa is to make fall; sāqaṭa is to let things drop one after another.
extendedMeaning: When the Israelites 'regretted (suqiṭa fī aydīhim)' — literally 'it fell into their hands' (7:149). The deniers demanded, 'cause the sky to fall (tusqiṭa) on us in pieces' (17:92).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Not a leaf falls (tasquṭu) but He knows it' (6:59). 'Shake the trunk of the palm; it will drop (tusāqiṭ) on you fresh ripe dates' (19:25). 'Surely into trial they have fallen (saqaṭū)' (9:49).

primaryMeaning: To go before, to be past. Salafa is to have passed; salaf are those who went before; aslafa is to send something ahead.
extendedMeaning: 'There every soul will be tested by what it did previously (aslafat)' (10:30). Pharaoh's people were made 'a precedent (salafan) and an example' (43:56).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times, often in 'except what has already passed (mā qad salafa)' — past deeds forgiven after a prohibition (2:275; 4:22). 'Eat and drink … for what you sent before you (aslaftum) in the days past' (69:24).

primaryMeaning: The broad side of something — the flat of the face or a page. Ṣafaḥa is to turn the side of one's face away — to overlook a wrong and let it pass.
extendedMeaning: 'If you pardon, overlook (taṣfaḥū) and forgive, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful' (64:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Pardon and overlook (wa-ṣfaḥū) until Allah brings His command' (2:109). 'Let them pardon and overlook (wal-yaṣfaḥū); do you not love that Allah should forgive you?' (24:22). 'Overlook with gracious forbearance (al-ṣafḥa al-jamīl)' (15:85).

primaryMeaning: To be hard and firm. Ṣulb is the backbone or loins; ṣalaba is to crucify — to stretch someone out on something hard.
extendedMeaning: Forbidden are 'the wives of your sons who are from your own loins (aṣlābikum)' (4:23). Yusuf told his fellow prisoner, 'the other will be crucified (fa-yuṣlabu)' (12:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him (ṣalabūhu)' — ʿĪsā (4:157). Pharaoh threatened, 'I will surely crucify you (la-uṣallibannakum) on the trunks of palm trees' (20:71). Man is created 'from between the backbone (al-ṣulb) and the ribs' (86:7).

primaryMeaning: A sound, a voice. Ṣawt is the sound one makes; aṣwāt are voices.
extendedMeaning: 'Incite whoever you can among them with your voice (bi-ṣawtika)' — said to Satan (17:64).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Lower your voice (min ṣawtika); the most hateful of sounds is the voice of the donkey' (31:19). 'Do not raise your voices (aṣwātakum) above the voice (ṣawti) of the Prophet' (49:2). 'Voices (al-aṣwāt) will be humbled before the Most Merciful' (20:108).

primaryMeaning: To be low and humble. Taḍarruʿ is humble pleading — lowering oneself before Allah; ḍarīʿ is a bitter thorny plant, a food of the Fire.
extendedMeaning: 'They will have no food except from a bitter thorny plant (ḍarīʿ)' (88:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Call on your Lord humbly (taḍarruʿan) and privately' (7:55). Allah seized nations with hardship 'so that they might humble themselves (yataḍarraʿūn)' (6:42). 'Why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves (taḍarraʿū)?' (6:43).

primaryMeaning: To wound the root of something — to hamstring an animal by cutting its legs. ʿĀqir, 'barren', is classically explained as one whose root of childbearing is cut.
extendedMeaning: 'They called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung (fa-ʿaqara)' (54:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. Thamud 'hamstrung her (fa-ʿaqarūhā)' — the she-camel of Salih (11:65; 91:14). Zakariyya said, 'My wife is barren (ʿāqirun)' (3:40).

primaryMeaning: To live. ʿAysh is life; maʿīsha and maʿāsh are livelihood — the means of living.
extendedMeaning: 'He will be in a pleasant life (ʿīshatin rāḍiya)' (69:21; 101:7). 'We have divided among them their livelihood (maʿīshatahum)' (43:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'We made for you therein means of livelihood (maʿāyish)' (7:10). 'Whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a narrow life (maʿīshatan ḍankā)' (20:124). 'We made the day for livelihood (maʿāshā)' (78:11).

primaryMeaning: To remain after others have gone — and dust, what is left behind. Ghābir is one who remains; ghabara is dust.
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times, mostly for Lut's wife, who 'was of those who remained behind (al-ghābirīn)' (7:83). On the Day of Judgment, 'faces that Day will have dust (ghabaratun) on them' (80:40).

primaryMeaning: To go ahead of others, to overstep — to fall short by neglect or to go too far. Farraṭa is to neglect; faraṭa is to act hastily; furuṭ is excess.
extendedMeaning: Musa and Harun feared Pharaoh would 'hasten (yafruṭa) against us' (20:45). 'Do not obey one … whose affair is in excess (furuṭan)' (18:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'We have not neglected (farraṭnā) anything in the Book' (6:38). 'Alas, our regret over what we neglected (farraṭnā)' (6:31). A soul will say, 'Alas, for what I neglected (farraṭtu) in regard to Allah' (39:56).

primaryMeaning: A grave. Qabr is a grave; qubūr are graves; aqbara is to give a grave.
extendedMeaning: 'He caused him to die and provided a grave for him (fa-aqbarahu)' (80:21). The Prophet was told not to stand 'at his grave (qabrihi)' — a hypocrite (9:84).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Allah will resurrect those in the graves (al-qubūr)' (22:7). 'When the graves (al-qubūr) are overturned' (82:4). 'Competition for more distracted you until you visited the graves (al-maqābir)' (102:2).

primaryMeaning: To impose something hard — to lay a charge on someone. Kallafa is to burden or charge; mutakallif is one who pretends, burdening himself with what he is not.
extendedMeaning: 'I do not ask you for any payment, and I am not of the pretenders (al-mutakallifīn)' (38:86).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'Allah does not burden (lā yukallifu) a soul beyond its capacity' (2:286). 'We do not charge (nukallifu) any soul except with what it can bear' (6:152). 'Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it' (65:7).

primaryMeaning: To be fine and subtle — too delicate to be seen — and gentle. Al-Laṭīf is the Subtle, who knows the finest details and is gentle with His servants; talaṭṭafa is to act with care.
extendedMeaning: The youths told their messenger, 'let him be cautious (wal-yatalaṭṭaf)' (18:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. 'He is the Subtle (al-laṭīf), the All-Aware' (6:103; 67:14). 'My Lord is subtle (laṭīfun) in what He wills' (12:100). 'Allah is Subtle (laṭīfun) with His servants' (42:19).

primaryMeaning: To come down, to descend from a height. Habaṭa is to go down; ihbiṭ is 'go down'.
extendedMeaning: Some stones 'fall down (yahbiṭu) out of fear of Allah' (2:74). Nuh was told, 'Descend (ihbiṭ) in peace from Us' (11:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. Adam, his wife and Iblis were told, 'Go down (ihbiṭū), as enemies to one another' (2:36). Iblis was told, 'Go down (fa-hbiṭ) from it; it is not for you to be arrogant here' (7:13). The Israelites were told, 'Go down (ihbiṭū) to any town' (2:61).

primaryMeaning: Heaviness — heavy rain, and heavy consequences. Wābil is a downpour; wabāl is the bad consequence of a deed; wabīl is ruinous.
extendedMeaning: 'They tasted the bad consequence (wabāla) of their affair' (59:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 8 times. Those who break the rules of hunting in iḥrām 'taste the consequence (wabāla) of their deed' (5:95). Charity for Allah is like 'a garden on high ground; heavy rain (wābilun) falls on it' (2:265). Pharaoh was seized 'with a ruinous (wabīlan) seizure' (73:16).

primaryMeaning: The root joins two senses: treating a wound, and uswa, a model to follow. Asiya is to grieve, sorrow that needs healing.
extendedMeaning: 'So that you not grieve (ta'saw) over what has escaped you' (57:23). Shuʿayb said, 'How could I grieve (āsā) over a disbelieving people?' (7:93).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'In the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example (uswatun ḥasana)' (33:21), as in Ibrahim (60:4). 'Do not grieve (lā ta'sa) over the defiantly disobedient people' (5:26).

primaryMeaning: To cut short what is due — to give less than something is worth. Bakhs is diminishing or cheating; bakhs also means very low in price.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever believes in his Lord will fear neither loss (bakhsan) nor burden' (72:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. Shuʿayb said, 'Do not deprive (lā tabkhasū) people of their things' (7:85). Yusuf was sold 'for a very low (bakhsin) price' (12:20). The debtor should 'not diminish (lā yabkhas) anything of it' (2:282).

primaryMeaning: To appear and stand out. Burj is a tower — a building that stands out — and a constellation; tabarruj is displaying one's beauty openly.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not display yourselves (lā tabarrajna) as in the display (tabarruja) of the former ignorance' (33:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'We have placed constellations (burūjan) in the sky' (15:16). 'By the sky with its constellations (al-burūj)' (85:1). 'Wherever you are, death will overtake you, even in lofty towers (burūjin)' (4:78).

primaryMeaning: To flash and shine. Barq is lightning; bariqa is for the eyes to be dazzled; ibrīq is a gleaming jug.
extendedMeaning: 'When the sight is dazzled (bariqa)' — on the Day of Resurrection (75:7). In Paradise, 'cups and jugs (abārīq)' (56:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'It is He who shows you lightning (al-barq), in fear and hope' (13:12; 30:24). In the parable of the hypocrites, 'the lightning (al-barqu) almost snatches away their sight' (2:20).

primaryMeaning: A piece cut off. Biḍāʿa is goods or merchandise — a portion of wealth set aside for trade; biḍʿ is 'a few', between three and nine.
extendedMeaning: The Romans will overcome 'within a few (biḍʿi) years' (30:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times, mostly in the story of Yusuf: travellers hid him 'as merchandise (biḍāʿatan)' (12:19), and his brothers found 'their merchandise (biḍāʿatahum) returned to them' (12:65). Yusuf remained in prison 'several (biḍʿa) years' (12:42).

primaryMeaning: A husband or master — one who owns and stands over. Baʿl is a husband; buʿūla are husbands; Baʿl is also the name of an idol.
extendedMeaning: Ilyas asked, 'Do you call on Baal (baʿlan) and forsake the best of creators?' (37:125).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'Their husbands (buʿūlatuhunna) have more right to take them back' (2:228). Women may show their adornment 'to their husbands (li-buʿūlatihinna)' (24:31). Sarah said, 'This is my husband (baʿlī), an old man' (11:72).

primaryMeaning: To weep, to shed tears. Bukā' is weeping; abkā is to make weep.
extendedMeaning: 'The heaven and the earth did not weep (bakat) for them' — Pharaoh's people (44:29). Yusuf's brothers came 'at nightfall, weeping (yabkūn)' (12:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'It is He who makes laugh and makes weep (abkā)' (53:43). The prophets 'fell down in prostration, weeping (bukiyyan)' (19:58). The people of knowledge 'fall on their faces weeping (yabkūna)' (17:109).

primaryMeaning: Nine. Tisʿa is nine; tisʿūn is ninety.
extendedMeaning: 'This is my brother; he has ninety-nine (tisʿun wa tisʿūna) ewes' (38:23). 'There were in the city nine (tisʿatu) men causing corruption' (27:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'We gave Musa nine (tisʿa) clear signs' (17:101). 'Over it are nineteen (tisʿata ʿashar)' — the keepers of Hell (74:30). The people of the Cave stayed three hundred years 'and added nine (tisʿan)' (18:25).

primaryMeaning: A rope — something that binds and connects. Ḥabl is a rope or a bond; ḥabl al-warīd is the jugular vein.
extendedMeaning: 'Their ropes (ḥibāluhum) and staffs seemed to him to be moving' (20:66). Around the neck of Abu Lahab's wife 'is a rope (ḥablun) of palm fibre' (111:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'Hold fast to the rope (bi-ḥabli) of Allah all together' (3:103). Humiliation is on them 'except with a rope (bi-ḥablin) from Allah and a rope from the people' (3:112). 'We are nearer to him than his jugular vein (ḥabl al-warīd)' (50:16).

primaryMeaning: A share or portion that falls to someone — a lot in life. Ḥaẓẓ is a share, or good fortune.
extendedMeaning: Of repelling evil with good: 'none is granted it except one of great fortune (ḥaẓẓin ʿaẓīm)' (41:35). Qarun's admirers said, 'He is of great fortune (ḥaẓẓin)' (28:79).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'For the male, the like of the share (ḥaẓẓi) of two females' (4:11). 'Allah intends to give them no portion (ḥaẓẓan) in the Hereafter' (3:176). 'They forgot a portion (ḥaẓẓan) of what they were reminded of' (5:13).

primaryMeaning: To snatch, to seize something quickly in passing. Khaṭifa is to grab; takhaṭṭafa is to carry off.
extendedMeaning: Whoever associates with Allah is like one who fell from the sky 'and the birds snatched him (takhṭafuhu)' (22:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'The lightning almost snatches away (yakhṭafu) their sight' (2:20). 'You feared that people might do away with you (yatakhaṭṭafakum)' (8:26). The devils are shot at 'except one who snatches (khaṭifa) a snatch (al-khaṭfa)' (37:10).

primaryMeaning: To cover. Khamr, 'wine', is what covers the mind; khimār is a head-covering.
extendedMeaning: 'Let them draw their head-covers (bi-khumurihinna) over their chests' (24:31). Yusuf's fellow prisoner dreamt, 'I am pressing wine (khamran)' (12:36).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'They ask you about wine (al-khamr) and gambling; say, in them is great sin' (2:219). 'Wine (al-khamr), gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination' (5:90). Paradise has 'rivers of wine (khamrin), delicious to drinkers' (47:15).

primaryMeaning: To pound and flatten, to crush something level with the ground. Dakk is crushing; dakkā' is levelled flat.
extendedMeaning: 'The earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed (fa-dukkatā) with a single crushing' (69:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. When Allah appeared to the mountain, 'He made it crumble to dust (dakkan)' (7:143). 'When the earth is pounded to dust, pounded and pounded (dakkan dakkā)' (89:21). The barrier of Dhu al-Qarnayn will be 'made level (dakkā')' (18:98).

primaryMeaning: The olive and its oil. Zaytūn is the olive tree; zayt is olive oil.
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'By the fig and the olive (wal-zaytūn)' (95:1). The lamp 'is lit from a blessed olive tree (zaytūnatin), neither of the east nor the west, whose oil (zaytuhā) would almost glow' (24:35). The olive is among the plants brought forth by rain (6:99).

primaryMeaning: To let livestock out to graze freely. Sarraḥa is to send away, to release — used for releasing a wife in divorce.
extendedMeaning: 'For you there is beauty in them when you bring them in and when you send them out to pasture (tasraḥūna)' — livestock (16:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'Divorce is twice; then either keep in kindness or release (tasrīḥun) with good treatment' (2:229). 'Release them (sarriḥūhunna) in kindness' (2:231). 'I will release you (usarriḥkunna) with a gracious release (sarāḥan jamīlā)' (33:28).

primaryMeaning: To close off. Sukr is intoxication, which closes off the mind; sakra is a stupor; sukkira is for the eyes to be blocked, dazzled.
extendedMeaning: 'From the fruits of the palm and grapes you take intoxicant (sakaran) and good provision' (16:67). The deniers would say, 'Our eyes have been dazzled (sukkirat)' (15:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated (sukārā)' (4:43). On that Day 'you will see people as if intoxicated (sukārā), but they are not intoxicated' (22:2). 'The stupor (sakratu) of death will come with the truth' (50:19).

primaryMeaning: The brightness of morning, when the sun is well up. Ḍuḥā is late morning; ḍaḥiya is to be exposed to the sun.
extendedMeaning: In Paradise Adam would 'not be thirsty nor suffer the sun's heat (taḍḥā)' (20:119). Musa's meeting was set for 'when the people gather in the forenoon (ḍuḥan)' (20:59).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'By the morning brightness (wal-ḍuḥā)' (93:1). 'By the sun and its brightness (ḍuḥāhā)' (91:1). 'Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come to them in the morning (ḍuḥan) while they play?' (7:98).

primaryMeaning: A wind that blows hard and sweeps things away. ʿĀṣif is stormy; ʿaṣf is the dry husk of grain, blown away by the wind.
extendedMeaning: 'Grain with husk (dhū al-ʿaṣf) and fragrant plants' (55:12). 'By the winds that blow violently (al-ʿāṣifāt)' (77:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'A stormy (ʿāṣifun) wind comes to them' — the ship at sea (10:22). The deeds of the deniers are 'like ashes on which the wind blows hard on a stormy (ʿāṣifin) day' (14:18). The Abraha army was made 'like straw (ka-ʿaṣfin) eaten up' (105:5).

primaryMeaning: To tie a knot — and so to make a firm contract. ʿUqda is a knot; ʿaqd is a contract; ʿaqqada is to bind by oath.
extendedMeaning: Musa prayed, 'untie the knot (ʿuqdatan) from my tongue' (20:27). 'From the evil of those who blow on knots (al-ʿuqad)' (113:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'O you who believe, fulfil your contracts (bil-ʿuqūd)' (5:1). 'Allah will hold you to account for what you bound by oath (ʿaqqadtum)' (5:89). 'Do not resolve on the knot (ʿuqdata) of marriage until the term ends' (2:235).

primaryMeaning: To cling and hang on to something. ʿAlaqa is a clinging clot — the embryo attached to the womb; muʿallaqa is left hanging.
extendedMeaning: Of a husband with more than one wife: 'do not incline wholly, leaving her as if hanging (kal-muʿallaqa)' (4:129).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times, mostly in the stages of creation: 'He created man from a clinging substance (ʿalaq)' (96:2), and 'We made the drop into a clinging clot (ʿalaqatan)' (23:14).

primaryMeaning: To support and prop up — and to aim at something deliberately. ʿAmad are pillars; taʿammada is to intend; mutaʿammid is deliberate.
extendedMeaning: 'Iram, with lofty pillars (al-ʿimād)' (89:7). The Fire is shut upon them 'in extended columns (ʿamadin)' (104:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'Allah raised the heavens without pillars (ʿamadin) that you can see' (13:2). 'Whoever kills a believer intentionally (mutaʿammidan), his recompense is Hell' (4:93). 'There is no blame on you for mistakes, but for what your hearts intended (taʿammadat)' (33:5).

primaryMeaning: To wander in confusion, unable to see the way — a blindness of the mind.
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times, always as yaʿmahūn, 'wandering blindly': 'Allah leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly (yaʿmahūn)' (2:15). 'Whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him, and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly' (7:186).

primaryMeaning: To scoop up with the hand. Ghurfa is a scoop of water — and a high chamber, an upper room raised above others.
extendedMeaning: 'They will be in the high dwellings (al-ghurufāt), secure' (34:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. Talut's army was tested by a river: 'except one who takes a scoop (ghurfatan) with his hand' (2:249). The God-conscious 'will have lofty mansions (ghurafun), above them mansions built high' (39:20). The servants of the Most Merciful 'will be rewarded with the Chamber (al-ghurfa)' (25:75).

primaryMeaning: To return. Fā'a is to come back; fay' is shade that returns after the sun passes, and wealth that returns to the Muslims without fighting; afā'a is to grant such wealth.
extendedMeaning: 'Their shadows incline (yatafayya'u) to the right and the left, prostrating to Allah' (16:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 7 times. 'What Allah gave (afā'a) to His Messenger from them' — wealth taken without battle (59:6). If fighting believers do not make peace, fight the aggressor 'until it returns (tafī'a) to the command of Allah' (49:9). Those who swear off their wives: 'if they return (fā'ū), Allah is Forgiving' (2:226).
'Their hearts hardened (qasat).' Qaswah is hardness. Qasi is hard-hearted.
notes: Hard hearts do not accept guidance.

quranUsage: Makatha means to stay. 'I will stay (amkuthu) at the fire.' Mukth is staying.
'Waves (mawj) like mountains.' Mawj is wave.
notes: The flood came with mountain-like waves.

quranUsage: 'They became regretful (nadimin).' Nadm is regret. Nadim is companion.
notes: Regret on Judgment Day will be too late.

quranUsage: Nusuk (نسك) is worship/sacrifice. 'My prayer and my nusuk (sacrifice).' Mansak is ritual.
'Half (nisf) of what they left.' Nisf is half. Insaf is fairness.
notes: Spouses inherit half in certain cases.

quranUsage: Nakatha means to break. 'Whoever breaks (nakatha) only harms himself.' Nakth is breaking oath.
Naqah (ناقة) is she-camel. 'This is the she-camel (naqah) of Allah.' The she-camel of Salih.
notes: The miraculous she-camel of Prophet Salih.

quranUsage: Wa'a means to preserve. 'That a preserving ear (udhunun wa'iyah) might preserve it.' Wi'a' is vessel.
Adda means to deliver. 'Deliver (addu) the trusts to their owners.' Ada' is performance.

extendedMeaning: Capturing, prisoners of war, and family ties.
quranUsage: 'They feed the captive (asir).' Asir is captive. Usrah is family.
notes: Treating captives well is commanded.

extendedMeaning: Being mute or unable to articulate truth.
quranUsage: 'Deaf, dumb (bukm), blind' describes those who reject truth.
notes: Spiritual dumbness is inability to speak truth.

quranUsage: Tabbara means to destroy. 'We destroyed (tabbarna) what Fir'awn and his people made.' Tatbir is destruction.
Thaqifa means to find/seize. 'Wherever you find (thaqiftumuhum) them.' Thaqif is a tribe.
Hibr is ink. Ahbar are scholars (rabbis). Hubur is joy.
notes: Scholars are associated with ink - the tools of knowledge.

extendedMeaning: Edge, side, letter, or distorting meaning.
quranUsage: Harf (حرف) is edge/letter. 'On an edge (harf) - if good comes to him...' Tahrif is distortion.
'When Isa sensed (ahassa) disbelief from them.' Hiss is sense. Ihsas is perception.
notes: The prophets had keen spiritual perception.

quranUsage: 'Except a little which you will store (tahsudun).' Hasad is harvest.
notes: Seven years of harvest stored for famine.

quranUsage: Hasara means to confine. 'If you are confined (uhsirtum).' Hasr is siege.
Hutamah (حطمة) is crusher - a name of Hell. 'It is the Hutamah.' Hattama is to crush.
notes: One of the names of Hell.

quranUsage: 'Mountains of various colors - white, red (humr), and black.' Ahmar is red. Himar is donkey.
notes: Red is mentioned in describing mountains and other natural phenomena.

quranUsage: 'It will be heated (yuhma) in the fire of Hell.' Hamy is heating. Himayah is protection.
notes: Gold and silver hoarded will be heated and used to brand.

quranUsage: 'They mixed (khalatu) good deeds with bad.' Khalt is mixing.
notes: Some mix good and bad deeds together.

quranUsage: Da'b (دأب) is custom. 'Like the custom (da'bi) of the people of Nuh.'

extendedMeaning: Studying and learning through repetition. Also means to wear away/efface.
quranUsage: 'By what you have been teaching (tadrusuna) of the Book.' Dars is lesson.
notes: Madrasah (school) comes from this root.

quranUsage: Dhara'a means to spread/create. 'He scattered (dhara'a) in it creatures.' Dhurriyyah is offspring.
Rada/yarda means to perish. 'He who perishes (halaka) from clear evidence.'

extendedMeaning: Watching, lying in wait, or observing.
quranUsage: Rasada means to watch. 'Your Lord is in wait (bil-mirsad).' Mirsad is ambush/watch.
Zajara means to rebuke. 'They were rebuked (zujiru).' Zajr is rebuke.
'When the earth is shaken (zulzilat).' Zalzalah is earthquake.
notes: Surah Az-Zalzalah describes the final earthquake.

extendedMeaning: Deliberate falsehood and fabrication. Also means visiting (turning towards someone).
quranUsage: 'Avoid false testimony (zur).' Zur is false testimony. Ziyara is visit.
notes: False testimony (shahadat al-zur) is a major sin.

quranUsage: 'A barrier (sadd) behind them.' Sadd is barrier. Sadid is correct.
notes: Barriers block and correct speech hits the mark.

extendedMeaning: Healing, curing disease, and providing remedy.
quranUsage: 'We reveal from the Quran what is healing (shifa').' 'When I am ill, He heals (yashfi) me.'
notes: The Quran is described as a healing.

quranUsage: 'In a cry (sarrah).' Sarrah is cry/scream. Israr is persistence.
notes: The old woman cried out in amazement.

quranUsage: 'When you have left ihram, then hunt (istadu).' Sayd is hunting/game.
notes: Hunting is forbidden during ihram pilgrimage state.

quranUsage: Daw' (ضوء) is light. 'Its daw' (light) would almost illuminate.' Diya' is radiance.
'Has the story of Ibrahim's honored guests (dayf) reached you?' Dayf is guest.
notes: Honoring guests is a prophetic tradition.

extendedMeaning: Debt, fine, penalty, or financial loss.
quranUsage: Gharam (غرام) is penalty. 'Its punishment is gharam (lasting).' Gharim is debtor.
'From clay like pottery (fakhkhar).' Fakhkhar is pottery. Fakhr is pride.
notes: Pottery is shaped from humble clay.

quranUsage: 'Reclining on beds (furush) lined with brocade.' Firash is bed. Farsh is carpet.
notes: The earth is spread like a carpet for humanity.

primaryMeaning: empty, to be free, to pour
extendedMeaning: Being empty, free (from occupation), and pouring out.
quranUsage: 'When you are free (faraghta), strive in worship.' Faragh is emptiness.
notes: Free time should be devoted to worship.

quranUsage: 'The greatest terror (faza') will not grieve them.' Faza' is terror.
notes: Believers are safe from the terror of Judgment Day.

extendedMeaning: Intention, purpose, and moderation in path.
quranUsage: 'Upon Allah is the moderate way (qasd al-sabil).' Qasd is intention. Maqsud is intended.
notes: Actions are judged by intentions (niyyat).

quranUsage: 'They brought his shirt (qamis) with false blood.' - Yusuf's shirt.
notes: Yusuf's shirt appears multiple times in his story.

quranUsage: 'Do not be of those who despair (qanitin).' Qunut is utter despair.
notes: Similar to ya's but more intense - complete giving up on Allah's help.

quranUsage: 'A cup (ka's) from a flowing spring.' Ka's is cup.
notes: Cups of pure drink circulate in Paradise.

quranUsage: Karrar means to return. 'If only we could return (nuraddu).' Takrar is repetition.
Kathm (كظم) is suppressing. 'Those who suppress (kadhimin) their anger.' Kazim is one who suppresses.
Kalb is dog. 'Their dog stretching his forelegs' - People of the Cave.
notes: The dog of the Cave's companions is mentioned honorably.

quranUsage: 'When the youths retreated to the cave (kahf).' Kahf is cave.
notes: Surah Al-Kahf tells of the sleepers in the cave.

quranUsage: 'From them emerge pearls (lu'lu').' Lu'lu' is pearl.
notes: Pearls come from the sea - a sign of Allah's creation.

extendedMeaning: Deviating from truth, or a side grave.
quranUsage: Ilhad (إلحاد) is deviation. 'Those who deviate (yulhidun) concerning His names.' Lahd is grave niche.
'Those who have not yet joined (yalhaquu) them.' Luhooq is catching up.
notes: Later generations will join the earlier ones.

quranUsage: 'In a Preserved Tablet (lawh mahfuz).' Lawh is tablet. Alwah is tablets.
notes: The Lawh al-Mahfuz contains all that was and will be.

extendedMeaning: Coral, mixing, and letting loose to pasture.
quranUsage: 'Pearls and coral (marjan).' Marjan is coral.
notes: Pearls and coral emerge from the meeting of two seas.

quranUsage: Maqt (مقت) is hatred. 'Great is maqt (hatred) with Allah.' Maqata is to abhor.
Amhala means to give time. 'Give respite (amhilhum) to the disbelievers.' Muhlah is respite.
'Those who follow desires want you to incline (tamilu).' Mayl is inclination.
notes: Inclining toward falsehood leads astray.

quranUsage: Nidd (ند) is rival/equal. 'Do not make rivals (andadan) to Allah.' Andad are equals.
Nazagha means to incite. 'Satan incites (yanzaghu) between them.' Nazgh is incitement.
Wati'a means to tread. 'They do not tread (yata'uuna) upon anything.' Wat' is treading.
Ara'ik (أرائك) are couches. 'Reclining on ara'ik (couches).'
Asifa means to grieve. 'Grieved (asifan).' Āsafūnā means angered us.
'We said: O fire, be cool (bardan) and safe for Ibrahim.' Barad is hail.
notes: Fire became cool for Ibrahim by Allah's command.

extendedMeaning: Strong dislike or aversion. The opposite of love.
quranUsage: Bughd (hatred) for the sake of Allah is part of faith. Hatred of truth leads to misguidance.
notes: Hating what Allah hates is part of complete faith.

quranUsage: Mublis (مبلس) is despairing. 'They will be in despair (mublisun).'
Bur (بور) is ruin. 'A people destroyed (buran).'
Thubur (ثبور) is destruction. 'They will call out destruction (thubura).'
Athara means to stir. 'Stirs up (tuthiru) the earth.'
Jathim means fallen. 'They became fallen (jathimin).'
Jala means to clear. 'When it clears (jallaha).'
Jawaza means to pass. 'We let pass (jawazna) the Children of Israel.'

extendedMeaning: The state of hunger and need for food.
quranUsage: 'Who fed them against hunger (ju').' 'We will test you with hunger (ju').'
notes: Hunger is both a test and a reminder of blessings.

quranUsage: Harīs (حريص) is eager. 'Eager (harīsan) for you.'

extendedMeaning: Envy - wishing removal of blessings from others.
quranUsage: 'From the evil of an envier (hasid) when he envies.' Hasad is envy.
notes: We seek refuge from the evil of enviers.

quranUsage: Hāsib (حاصب) is stoning wind. 'A storm of stones (hāsiban).'
Hut is whale. Yunus was swallowed by the whale (hut).
notes: Yunus is called Sahib al-Hut - companion of the whale.

quranUsage: Mahīs (محيص) is escape. 'There is no escape (mahīs).'
'They seek to deceive (yukhadi'un) Allah.' Khida' is deception.
notes: Hypocrites think they deceive Allah but deceive only themselves.

quranUsage: Kharrāsūn are liars. 'Destroyed are the liars (kharrāsūn).'
Khutuwāt (خطوات) are steps. 'Do not follow the footsteps (khutuwāt) of Satan.'
'Forbidden to you is the flesh of swine (khinzir).' Khinzir is pig.
notes: Pork is forbidden (haram) in Islam.

quranUsage: Khāwiya means collapsed/empty. 'Its roofs collapsed (khāwiya).'
Khāba means to fail. 'He has failed (khāba) who carries injustice.'
Yadra'ūna means to ward off. 'They ward off (yadra'ūna) evil with good.'
Duhn (دهن) is oil. 'Oil (duhn) for eating.' Also: 'They wish you to compromise (tudhinu).'

extendedMeaning: Arm, forearm, and cubit (unit of measure).
quranUsage: 'A chain of seventy cubits (dhira').' Dhira' is arm/cubit.
notes: The cubit was measured by the forearm.

quranUsage: Dhimmah (ذمة) is covenant/protection. 'Neither kinship (dhimmah) nor covenant.'
'We strengthened (rabatna) her heart.' Rabt is tying. Ribat is bond/garrison.
notes: Allah ties and strengthens the hearts of believers.

quranUsage: 'We will cast terror (ru'b) into their hearts.' Ru'b is terror.
notes: Allah cast terror into enemy hearts at Badr.

quranUsage: 'Good companions (rafiq).' Rifq is gentleness. Rafiq is companion.
notes: The Prophet will be with the prophets as rafiq.

quranUsage: Zahaq means to perish. 'Falsehood is bound to perish (zahūqan).'
Asbāt (أسباط) are tribes/grandsons. 'The tribes (asbāt) of Israel.'
'One-sixth (sudus).' Sudus is one-sixth.
notes: Parents inherit one-sixth when there are children.

quranUsage: 'Seven ears (sanabil) of grain.' Sunbulah is ear of grain.
notes: Seven ears in Yusuf's dream and the parable of charity.

quranUsage: 'That Day people will proceed in scattered (ashtat) groups.' Shatat is dispersion.
notes: On Judgment Day, people emerge scattered from graves.

quranUsage: 'Whoever is protected from the stinginess (shuhh) of his soul.' Shuhh is miserliness.
notes: Stinginess of the soul must be overcome.

quranUsage: Sharaha means to open/expand. 'Did We not expand (nashrah) your breast?'

extendedMeaning: Legislating, ordained path, and Islamic law.
quranUsage: 'He has ordained (shara'a) for you the religion.' Shari'ah is divine law.
notes: Shari'ah is the path Allah ordained for humanity.

quranUsage: Shatr (شطر) is direction. 'Turn your face toward (shatra) the Sacred Mosque.'
Shihāb (شهاب) is shooting star/flame. 'A piercing flame (shihāb).'
Sabba means to pour. 'We poured (sababnā) water.' Sabbān is pouring.
