Isda' means to proclaim. 'Proclaim (isda') what you are commanded.'
Asdafa means to turn away. 'He who turns away (asdafa).'
'They will cry out (yastasrikhun) therein.' Surakh is scream.
notes: The people of Hell will scream for help.

quranUsage: 'A yellow (safra') cow, bright in color.' Asfar is yellow. Safir is whistling.
notes: The cow in Surah Al-Baqarah was specifically bright yellow.

quranUsage: Sanam (صنم) is idol. 'The idols (asnām).' Ibrahim's prayer against idols.
Tatrud means to drive away. 'Do not drive away (tatrud) those who call upon their Lord.'
Tams means to obliterate. 'Obliterate (atims) their wealth.'
Tatwī means to roll up. 'We will roll up (natwī) the heaven.'
'Utbā is blamed/threshold. 'Ataba (عتب) is to blame.'
Ya'thaw means to cause mischief. 'Do not cause corruption (ta'thaw).'
'Usbah (عصبة) is a group. 'A group ('usbah) of them.'
'By time (al-'asr), mankind is in loss.' 'Asr is also afternoon prayer time.
notes: Surah Al-'Asr emphasizes the value of time.

quranUsage: 'Your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your paternal uncles ('amm).'
notes: Am is paternal uncle; 'amm is also general/common.

quranUsage: 'Anat (عنت) is hardship. 'Lest you fall into hardship ('anat).'
Istaghāthū means to seek help. 'If they seek help (yastaghīthū).' Ghawth is aid.
'You have come to Us alone (furada).' Fard is single. Munfarid is alone.
notes: Each person will come alone on Judgment Day.

quranUsage: Yafūtu means to escape. 'Nothing escapes (yafūtu) Him.'
Fawj (فوج) is group. 'In crowds (afwājan).' Surah An-Nasr.
Yaqturū means to be stingy. Qatara (قترة) is dust. 'Dust (qatara) will cover them.'
Qidd (قد) is cut/form. 'Cut (qudda) from behind.'
Qāri'ah (قارعة) is striking calamity. Surah Al-Qāri'ah. 'The Striking Hour (qāri'ah).'
Iqtarafa means to commit. 'What they committed (iqtarafū).'
Quswā (قصوى) is furthest. 'The furthest (quswā) side.'
Qutr (قطر) is region/molten metal. 'From the regions (aqtār) of the heavens.'
Taqfu means to follow. 'Do not follow (taqfu) what you have no knowledge of.'
Inkasafat means eclipsed. 'When the moon is eclipsed (inkasafat).' (Also kasf: fragments)
'We clothed (kasawna) the bones with flesh.' Kiswa is clothing.
notes: Allah clothed bones with flesh in creation.

quranUsage: 'Today I have completed (akmaltu) your religion.' Kamal is perfection.
notes: Islam was perfected and completed.

quranUsage: 'A brilliant star (kawkab).' Kawkab is planet/star. Kawakib are planets.
notes: Yusuf saw eleven kawkab (stars/planets) prostrating to him.

quranUsage: Alzama means to make necessary. 'We have attached (alzamnāhu) to him.'

extendedMeaning: Physical touching and contact. Also seeking or attempting.
quranUsage: 'Or you have touched (lamastum) women' refers to physical contact. Also used for seeking (the sky).
notes: Lamasa can be a euphemism for intimacy.

quranUsage: Yalwūna means to twist. 'They twist (yalwūna) their tongues.'
'Speak to him with soft (layyin) speech.' Lin is softness.
notes: Musa was told to speak gently to Firawn.

quranUsage: Mārid (مارد) is rebellious. 'A rebellious (mārid) devil.'
Misr (مصر) is Egypt. 'Go down to Egypt (misr).'
'What has passed (ma mada) is past.' Madi is past.
notes: The past (al-madi) is gone; focus on future deeds.

quranUsage: Tamīda means to sway. 'Lest it sway (tamīda) with you.'
Yansifuhu means to scatter. 'He will scatter (yansifuhu) it.'
Nushūz (نشوز) is rebellion/disobedience. 'Those from whom you fear rebellion (nushūz).'
Nafida means to be exhausted. 'The sea would be exhausted (nafida).'
Anqadha means to save. 'He saved (anqadhakum) you from it.'
Nakal (نكال) is punishment/warning. 'A punishment (nakalan) from Allah.'
Huzzi means shake. 'Shake (huzzi) toward you the trunk.'
Uhilla means raised/dedicated. 'What has been dedicated (uhilla) to other than Allah.'
'Their hearts tremble (wajilat) when Allah is mentioned.' Wajal is trembling fear.
notes: Hearts of believers tremble at Allah's mention.

quranUsage: Yūza'ūn means restrained/driven. 'They will be driven (yūza'ūn).'

extendedMeaning: Being in the middle, moderate, best.
quranUsage: Wasat (وسط) is middle/best. 'A moderate (wasatan) nation.' 'In the midst (wasat) of them.'

extendedMeaning: Whispering evil suggestions. Satan's method of temptation.
quranUsage: 'From the evil of the whisperer (waswas).' Waswasah is Satan's whispering.
notes: Seeking refuge from waswasah is in Surah An-Nas.

quranUsage: Afala means to set. 'When it set (afala).'
Amad (أمد) is period. 'The period (amad) was prolonged.'

extendedMeaning: Creating something unprecedented. Can be praiseworthy or blameworthy.
quranUsage: Badi' is Originator of heavens and earth. Bid'ah in religion is condemned innovation.
notes: Allah creates without precedent; humans should not innovate in religion.

quranUsage: Balā' (بلاء) is test. 'A great trial (balā').' Yablū: to test.
Tabba means to perish. 'May the hands of Abu Lahab perish (tabbat).'
Jidar (جدار) is wall. 'A wall (jidar) about to collapse.'
'What you have earned (jarahtum) by day.' Jurh is wound. Iktisab is earning.
notes: Earning (good or bad) is like acquiring wounds on one's record.

quranUsage: Jasad (جسد) is body. 'A body (jasad) without soul.'
Jahhaza means to equip. 'When he equipped (jahhazahum) them.'
Ḥama' (حمأ) is mud. 'Black mud (ḥama') altered.'
Maḥīḍ (محيض) is menstruation. 'About menstruation (maḥīḍ).'
Takhriqu means to pierce. 'You will never pierce (takhriqa) the earth.'
Ikhsa'ū means be despised. 'Be despised (ikhsa'ū) in it.'
Khaṣāṣah (خصاصة) is need/poverty. 'Even if they have need (khaṣāṣah).'
'Lower (ikhfid) your wing to the believers.' Khafd is lowering.
notes: Lowering one's wing means being humble and gentle.

quranUsage: Madhūr means driven away. 'Driven away (madhūran).'
Dahd means refutation. 'To refute (yudḥiḍū) the truth.' Dāḥiḍah: slipping.
Dākhirūn are humiliated. 'They will enter humiliated (dākhirīna).'
Durrī (دري) is brilliant. 'A brilliant (durriyyun) star.' Darr: continuous flowing.
Dalw (دلو) is bucket. 'He let down his bucket (dalwahu).'
Rattil means to recite slowly. 'Recite (rattil) the Quran slowly.'
Rahuba means to be spacious. 'Despite its vastness (raḥubat).' Marhaban: welcome.

extendedMeaning: Departing, traveling, and loading for journey.
quranUsage: 'The journey (rihlah) of winter and summer.' Rihlah is journey. Rahil is departing.
notes: Quraysh's trade journeys to Yemen (winter) and Syria (summer).

quranUsage: Arādhil (أراذل) are lowly ones. 'The lowly (arādhilunā) among us.'
Tarqā means to ascend. 'You ascend (tarqā) in the sky.' Ruqyah: spell.
Tarkanu means to incline. 'Do not incline (tarkanū) to those who wrong.'
Zukhruf (زخرف) is adornment/gold. Surah Az-Zukhruf. 'Adorned (zukhruf) speech.'
'Satan made them slip (azallahuma).' Zallah is slip/error.
notes: Satan caused Adam and Hawwa to slip.

quranUsage: Tazūla means to cease. 'Lest they cease (tazūlā).'
Sijill (سجل) is record/scroll. 'Like a rolled scroll (sijill).'
Suht (سحت) is unlawful. 'Consumers of the unlawful (suht).'
'They followed what displeased (askhata) Allah.' Sakhat is displeasure.
notes: Following desires leads to Allah's displeasure.

quranUsage: 'At the Lote Tree (sidrah) of the utmost boundary.' Sidr is lote tree.
notes: Sidrat al-Muntaha marks the boundary of creation.

quranUsage: Sāribun means going forth. 'Going forth (sāribun) by day.'
'And made the sun a lamp (sirajan).' Siraj is lamp.
notes: The sun is described as a brilliant lamp.

quranUsage: Musāfihīn are fornicators. 'Not as fornicators (musāfihīn).' Safaha: shed blood.
'We carried them in the laden ship (safinah).' Safinah is ship.
notes: Nuh's ship (safinah) saved the believers from the flood.

quranUsage: 'The sky as a protected ceiling (saqf).' Saqf is roof.
notes: The sky is described as a protective ceiling.

quranUsage: Silāh (سلاح) is weapon. 'Take their weapons (aslihatahum).'
Sāmiran means conversing. 'Conversing (sāmiran) by night.'
Samm (سم) is hole/eye of needle. 'Through the eye (samm) of a needle.'
Simān (سمان) are fat. 'Seven fat (simān) cows.'
Sawwala means to entice. 'Your souls enticed (sawwalat) you.'
'A flood (sayl) came upon them.' Sayl is flood/flow. Sayil is flowing.
notes: The flood of 'Arim destroyed the dam.

quranUsage: Sha'n (شأن) is affair. 'He is upon a matter (sha'n).' 'Every person has a concern (sha'n).'
Shūrā (شورى) is consultation. Surah Ash-Shūrā. 'Consult (shāwirhum) them.'

extendedMeaning: Elder, old age, and respected scholar.
quranUsage: 'Our father is an old man (shaykh).' Shaykh is elder/scholar.
notes: Shaykh denotes age, wisdom, and religious authority.

quranUsage: Sarh (صرح) is palace. 'A palace (sarhan) lofty.'

extendedMeaning: Dry clay that makes a ringing sound.
quranUsage: 'From clay (salsal) like pottery.' Salsal is dried clay.
notes: Final stage of clay before life was breathed in.

quranUsage: Tabaq (طبق) is layer. 'In layers (tabaqan) upon layers.'
Tifl (طفل) is child. 'Or children (tifl) not aware.'
Talab is seeking. Talib is seeker/student. 'Seeking (yatlubu) the life of this world.'
notes: Talib al-'ilm is seeker of knowledge.

quranUsage: Tawq (طوق) is collar. 'Collared (yutawwaqūna) with what they withheld.' Yutīqūna: able.
A'jamī (أعجمي) is non-Arabic. 'A foreign (a'jamī) Quran?'

extendedMeaning: Chastity, modesty, and abstaining from forbidden.
quranUsage: 'Let those who cannot marry keep chaste (yasta'fifu).' 'Iffah is chastity.
notes: Chastity is highly praised in Islam.

quranUsage: 'Aqīm (عقيم) is barren. 'A barren ('aqīm) wind.' 'I am barren ('aqim).'
'Awrah (عورة) is nakedness/vulnerable. 'Our houses are exposed ('awrah).'
Ghasaq (غسق) is darkness. 'The darkness (ghasaq) of night.'
'If you are in a state of major impurity, purify yourselves.' Ghusl is ritual bath.
notes: Ghusl is required after certain states for prayer.

quranUsage: Yaghuddu means to lower. 'Lower (ughdudd) your voice.' 'Lower (yaghuddu) their gaze.'
Ghamrah (غمرة) is covering/flood. 'In their flood (ghamratihim) of ignorance.'
Ghawran (غورا) is sinking/deep. 'Its water becomes sunken (ghawran).'
'He sends down the rain (ghayth).' Ghayth is saving rain.
notes: Ghayth implies rain that relieves drought - a mercy.

quranUsage: Tafshalū means to fail. 'Lest you fail (tafshalū).'
'Splitter (Faliq) of the seed.' Falaq is daybreak/splitting.
notes: Surah Al-Falaq - The Daybreak. Seeds split to grow.

quranUsage: 'When Hell boils over (farat).' Fawran is immediately. Fawr is boiling.
notes: Hell boils and erupts with fury.

quranUsage: Qalā'id (قلائد) are necklaces/garlands. 'The garlanded (qalā'id) animals.'

extendedMeaning: Pen (originally a trimmed reed) for writing.
quranUsage: 'By the pen (qalam) and what they write.' Al-Qalam is Surah 68.
notes: The pen was among the first things created.

quranUsage: Qanātīr (قناطير) are heaps. 'Heaps (qanātīr) of gold and silver.'
Karb (كرب) is distress. 'We saved him from the distress (karb).'

extendedMeaning: Ankle, cube shape, and the Kaaba.
quranUsage: 'To the ankles (ka'bayn).' Ka'b is ankle. Ka'bah is cube-shaped.
notes: The Kaaba is cube-shaped. Feet are washed to the ankles.

quranUsage: Akwāb (أكواب) are cups. 'With cups (akwāb) and jugs.'
'Darkness in a deep sea (lujji).' Lujjah is deep sea.
notes: Disbelief is like being in deep, dark waters.

quranUsage: Yalmizūna means to criticize. 'Those who criticize (yalmizūna).' Lumazah is slanderer.
Al-Majid (The Glorious) is Allah's name. 'Quran Majid' - Glorious Quran.
notes: Majid implies glorious and generous together.

quranUsage: Mazzaqnā means to tear apart. 'We tore them (mazzaqnāhum) apart.'
Mahīn (مهين) is contemptible. 'From water contemptible (mahīn).'
Yamīzu means to distinguish. 'Until He distinguishes (yamīza) the evil from the good.'
Tanhitūn means to carve. 'You carve (tanhitūn) houses from mountains.'
Nansakh means to abrogate. 'What We abrogate (nansakh) of a verse.'
Nasl (نسل) is offspring. Yansilūn means they hasten. 'They hasten (yansilūn).'
Nāsiya (ناصية) is forelock. 'A lying, sinful forelock (nāsiya).'
Na'jah (نعجة) is ewe. 'Ninety-nine ewes (na'jah).'
Anfāl (أنفال) are spoils. Surah Al-Anfāl. Nāfilah is extra prayer.
Naqīr (نقير) is speck. 'Not even a speck (naqīran).' Also: nāqūr (trumpet).

extendedMeaning: Ant - example of small yet organized creature.
quranUsage: An-Naml (The Ant) is Surah 27. An ant warned others of Sulaiman's army.
notes: Ants show organization and communication.

quranUsage: Hātū means bring. 'Bring (hātū) your proof.'
Hanī'an (هنيئا) is pleasant/wholesome. 'Eat it pleasantly (hanī'an).'
Hayyi' means to prepare. 'Prepare (hayyi') for us.'
Wadda'a means to leave. 'Your Lord has not left (wadda'aka) you.'
'They began to cover themselves with leaves (waraq).' Waraq is leaves/paper.
notes: Adam and Hawwa covered themselves with Paradise leaves.

quranUsage: Tawfīq (توفيق) is success. 'My success (tawfīqī) is only through Allah.'
'Stop (qif) them, they will be questioned.' Wuquf is standing (at Arafah).
notes: Standing at Arafah is the pillar of Hajj.

quranUsage: 'Green or dry (yabis)' - all recorded in a clear book. Yabis is dry.
notes: Nothing escapes Allah's knowledge - fresh or dry.

quranUsage: Ibil (إبل) is camels. 'Do they not look at the ibil (camels)?'
Ujaj (أجاج) is salty/bitter. 'And this is salty, bitter (ujaj).'
Azifah (آزفة) is the Approaching. 'The Approaching Day (azifah) has approached.'
Assasa means to found. 'One who founded (assasa) his building on taqwa.'
Isr (إصر) is burden. 'The burden (isr) that was upon them.'
Uff (أف) is an expression of disgust. 'Do not say to them uff.'
'On the clear horizon (ufuq).' Ufuq is horizon. Afaq are horizons/regions.
notes: The Prophet saw Jibril on the clear horizon.

quranUsage: 'The nose (anf) for a nose' - in retribution laws. Anifa means to disdain.
notes: Anf also relates to self-respect and pride.

quranUsage: 'Do not waste (tubaddhir) wastefully.' Badhr is seed. Tabdhir is wasting.
notes: Don't scatter resources wastefully.

quranUsage: Bariha means to cease. 'I will not cease (abrahu) until I reach.'
Barzakh (برزخ) is barrier. 'Between them is a barzakh (barrier).' Also the realm after death.
Bahij (بهيج) is beautiful. 'Pairs of every beautiful (bahij) kind.'
Bahimah (بهيمة) is beast. 'Bahimah (beast) of cattle.'
Related to destruction.
Ja'ara means to cry out. 'You cry out (taj'arun) to Him.'
'Every nation kneeling (jathiyah).' Juthuuw is kneeling.
notes: Surah Al-Jathiyah - nations kneeling before judgment.

quranUsage: Ajdath (أجداث) are graves. 'They come out from the graves (ajdath).'
'We will crucify you on the trunks (judhoo') of palm trees.' Jidh' is trunk.
notes: Pharaoh's magicians were threatened with crucifixion on palm trunks.

quranUsage: Juz' (جزء) is part. 'For each gate a part (juz') of them.'
Jayb (جيب) is pocket. 'Put your hand in your jayb (pocket).' Also collar.
Hadaqa means to stare. Hadiqah is garden.
Harrada means to urge. 'Urge (harrid) the believers.'
Hadda means to urge. 'You do not urge (tahadduna) feeding the poor.'
Hafiy (حفي) is well-informed. 'As if you were eager (hafiy) about it.'
Halaqa means to shave. 'Shaving (muhaliqin) your heads.'
Hajah (حاجة) is need. 'No need (hajah) in their hearts.'
Akhbata means to be humble. 'Those who humble (akhbatu) themselves.'
'If Allah forsakes (yakhdhul) you, who can help you?'
notes: Being abandoned by Allah is the worst fate.

quranUsage: 'Do not be loud in your prayer nor silent, but seek between.' Khaft is lowering voice.
notes: Moderation in voice during prayer is recommended.

quranUsage: 'Until the white thread (khayt) is distinct from the black.' Khayt is thread.
notes: Dawn is when white and black threads of light are distinguishable.

quranUsage: Yadu'u means to push. 'Repulses (yadu'u) the orphan.'
Dhi'b (ذئب) is wolf. 'The wolf (dhi'b) ate him.'
Dhirwah is peak. The highest point.
notes: Mountains have peaks that reach the sky.

quranUsage: Adhqan (أذقان) are chins. 'Fall on their chins (adhqan).'
Murdif means following. 'Followed (murdifin) by a thousand.'
Raghadan (رغدا) is plentifully. 'Eat plentifully (raghadan).'
'A written (marqum) register.' Raqm is number/writing.
notes: Our deeds are numbered and recorded precisely.

quranUsage: Rurkud means to run. 'When they were running (yarkudun).'
Rukam (ركام) is heaped. 'Heaped clouds (rukam).'
'Therein are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates (rumman).'
notes: Pomegranates are Paradise fruits.

quranUsage: Raht (رهط) is clan. 'Your clan (rahtuka) is powerful.'
Rahn (رهن) is pledge. 'A pledge (rihan) taken.'
Ragha means to turn aside. 'He turned (raga) to them.'
'As for the foam (zabad), it vanishes.' Zabad is foam.
notes: Falsehood is like foam - it appears but vanishes.

quranUsage: Yazji means to drive. 'Drives (yazji) clouds.'
'For them therein is sighing (zafir).' Zafir is sighing/groaning.
notes: The people of Hell sigh and groan.

quranUsage: Zaqqum (زقوم) is the tree in Hell. 'The tree of Zaqqum.'
Sa'ima means to be weary. 'They do not weary (yas'amun).'

extendedMeaning: Covering and concealing, especially faults or private matters.
quranUsage: Sitr is covering. Allah is As-Satir/As-Sittir who covers faults. Satr al-'awrah is covering private parts.
notes: Covering others' faults is praised.

quranUsage: Sujjirat means kindled. 'The seas are set ablaze (sujjirat).'
Saraabil are garments. 'Garments (saraabil).'
Naslakhu means to strip. 'We strip (naslakhu) from it the night.'
'A chain (silsilah) of seventy cubits.' Silsilah is chain.
notes: Chains bind the people of Hell.

quranUsage: 'From an extract (sulalah) of clay.' Sulalah is extract/lineage.
notes: Humans are created from an extract of clay.

quranUsage: Salwa (سلوى) is quail. 'The manna and salwa (quail).'
Yusīghuhu means can swallow. 'He can hardly swallow (yusīghuhu) it.'
Siha means to travel. 'Travel (sihu) four months.'
Ash'am is ill-fated. 'Most ill-fated (ash'aha).'
Mashun is laden. 'The laden (mashun) ship.'
Shatat (شطط) is excess. 'We said excessively (shatatan).'
'I only complain (ashku) of my grief to Allah.' Shakwa is complaint.
notes: Ya'qub complained only to Allah, not to people.

quranUsage: Shana'ana is hatred. 'Let not hatred (shana'anu) make you unjust.'
Shayb (شيب) is gray hair. 'My head has kindled with gray (shayban).'
Sabi'un (صابئون) are Sabians.
'The coloring (sibghah) of Allah.' Sibghah is dye/coloring.
notes: Islam is Allah's sibghah - His coloring of the soul.

quranUsage: Saba means to incline. 'I might incline (asbu) to them.'
'Even if it be inside a rock (sakhrah).' Sakhr is rock/boulder.
notes: Nothing is hidden from Allah, even inside solid rock.

quranUsage: 'A screaming wind (sarsar).' Sarsar is freezing violent wind.
notes: The 'Ad were destroyed by sarsar wind.

quranUsage: Sarim (صريم) is harvested. 'Like a garden harvested (sarim).'
'Their sides forsake their beds (madaji').' Daj' is lying down. Madja' is bed.
notes: The righteous leave their beds for night prayer.

quranUsage: Adghath (أضغاث) are confused dreams. 'Confused dreams (adghath).'
Taffa means to extinguish. 'They want to extinguish (yutfi'u).'
Tafiqa means to begin. 'They began (tafiqa) patching.'
Zama' (ظمأ) is thirst. 'No thirst (zama').'
'Abasa means to frown. 'He frowned ('abasa).' Surah 80.
'Urwah (عروة) is handhold. 'The firmest handhold ('urwah).'
'That he may expose (yubdi) their nakedness ('awrat).' 'Awrah is what must be covered.
notes: Adam and Hawwa's nakedness was exposed after eating from the tree.

quranUsage: 'Azzara means to honor. 'Honor ('azzaruhu) and help him.'
'Ir (عير) is caravan. 'Ask the caravan ('ir).'
Yafturu means to slacken. 'They do not slacken (yafturun).'
Fatil (فتيل) is thread. 'A thread (fatilan).'
Fajj (فج) is road. 'From every distant road (fajj).'
Farat is scattered. Related to scattering.
Istafziz means to disturb. 'Disturb (astafziz) whom you can.'
Tafsahu means to make room. 'Make room (tafsahu).'
'They said: We are missing (nafqidu) the king's cup.' Faqd is loss.
notes: Opposite of و-ج-د (finding).

quranUsage: Qabas (قبس) is firebrand. 'Or I find a firebrand (qabas).'
Qarḥ (قرح) is wound. 'If a wound (qarḥ) has touched you.'
Qiradah (قردة) is apes. 'Be apes (qiradatan) despised.'
Kubitu means suppressed. 'They were suppressed (kubitū).'
Kuwwirat means wrapped. 'When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat).'
Malja' (ملجأ) is refuge. 'No refuge (malja').'
Ladhdhah (لذة) is pleasure. 'A pleasure (ladhdhatan) for the drinkers.'
Talattafat means turned. Talfit: distraction.
Iltaffat means wrapped. 'When the legs are wrapped (iltaffat).'
Talaqqā means to receive. 'He received (talaqqā) from his Lord words.'
Talqaf means to swallow. 'It will swallow (talqaf) what they made.'
Lahab (لهب) is flame. Surah Al-Masad. 'Father of flame (lahab).'
Matīn (متين) is firm. 'The Possessor of Power, the Firm (matīn).'
Yamḥū means to erase. 'Allah erases (yamḥū) what He wills.'
Maraḥan is arrogant. 'Do not walk arrogantly (maraḥan).'
'A cup mixed (mizaj) with ginger.' Mazj is mixing.
notes: Paradise drinks are mixed with special flavors.

quranUsage: 'Then from a chewed lump (mudghah).' Mudghah is chewed substance.
notes: Stage of embryo resembling chewed flesh.

quranUsage: Tamūru means to sway. 'The earth will sway (tamūru).'
Yan'awna means to distance. 'They distance (yan'awna) from it.'
Intatharat means scattered. 'When the stars are scattered (intatharat).'

extendedMeaning: Copper/brass, and ill omen or misfortune.
quranUsage: 'Sent upon them a screaming wind in days of misfortune (nahisat).' Nuhas is copper.
notes: Copper and brass were important metals in ancient times.

quranUsage: 'They made between Him and the jinn a lineage (nasab).' Nasab is lineage.
notes: False claims of lineage between Allah and jinn are rejected.

quranUsage: Manḍūd means piled up. 'Bananas piled up (manḍūd).'
'Radiant (nadirah) faces.' Nadrah is radiance/bloom.
notes: Faces of the blessed will be radiant.

quranUsage: Tanfudhū means to pass through. 'If you can pass through (tanfudhū).'
Naqqabū means they explored. 'They explored (naqqabū) in the lands.'
Nukisū means reversed. 'Then they were reversed (nukisū).'
Yastankif means to disdain. 'Would never disdain (yastankifa).'
'They defeated (hazamu) them.' Hazimah is defeat.
notes: Armies are defeated by Allah's permission.

quranUsage: Muhṭi'īn means hastening with necks craned. 'Racing with heads raised (muhṭi'īna).'
Humazah (همزة) is slanderer. Surah Al-Humazah. 'Every slanderer (humazah).'
Awtād (أوتاد) are stakes. 'Pharaoh of the stakes (awtād).'
'By the odd (watr) and the even.' Witr is odd. Watar is string.
notes: Witr prayer has an odd number of units.

quranUsage: Wathan (وثن) is idol. 'The idols (awthān).'
Awjasa means to feel. 'He felt (awjasa) fear.'
Mu'ṣadah means closed. 'It is closed (mu'ṣadah) upon them.'
Athath (أثاث) is furniture. 'Furniture (athath) and enjoyment.'
Irbah (إربة) is need. 'Those without irbah (need) for women.'
Azara means to support. 'Strengthen (azirni) me.' Izar is waist-wrapper.
Azza means to incite. 'We sent devils to incite (ta'uzzuhum) them.'
Ashir (أشر) is proud. 'Is he the proud (ashir) liar?'
Related to expression of distress.
Amal (أمل) is hope. 'Let them hope (amal) extend their life.'
Amah (أمة) is maidservant. 'A believing slave girl (amah).'
Awwah (أواه) is one who sighs. 'Ibrahim was forbearing, awwah (sighing).'
Tabattul is devotion. 'Devote (tabattal) yourself to Him.'
Bakha'a means to destroy oneself. 'Will you destroy (bakhi') yourself?'
Badan (بدن) is body. 'Today We will save your body (badan).' Budn are sacrificial camels.
Abras (أبرص) is leper. 'I cure the abras (leper).'
Barima means to be weary. 'Have they decided (abramu) an affair?'
Bazagha means to rise. 'When the sun rose (bazaghat).'
Basara means to frown. 'Then he frowned (basara).'
Bussat means crumbled. 'The mountains will be crumbled (bussat).'

extendedMeaning: Being given up, detained for sin.
quranUsage: Ubsilat means to be detained. 'A soul detained (ubsilat) for what it earned.'
Batira means to be insolent. 'They were insolent (batirat) in their living.'
Bu'thira means to be scattered. 'When graves are scattered (bu'thirat).'
Ba'ir (بعير) is camel. 'A camel-load (ba'ir).'
Banan (بنان) is fingertips. 'Strike their fingertips (banan).'
At-Tawr (التور) can be related to Mount Tur.
Athkhana means to overcome. 'Until he has overcome (yuthkhina) in the land.'
'It became a serpent (thu'ban).' Thu'ban is large snake.
notes: Musa's staff became a great serpent.

quranUsage: Thaqib (ثاقب) is piercing. 'A piercing (thaqib) flame.'
Jubb (جب) is well. 'Cast him into the bottom of the well (jubb).'
Judhadhan means pieces. 'He made them into pieces (judhadhan).'
'We sent upon them locusts (jarad).' Jarad is locusts.
notes: Locusts stripped Egypt as a plague.

quranUsage: Juruz (جرز) is barren. 'A barren (juruz) land.'
'When evil touches him, he is impatient (jazu'an).' Jaza' is impatience.
notes: Impatience is the opposite of sabr (patience).

quranUsage: Jism (جسم) is body. 'Increased him in body (jism) and knowledge.'
Ajlib means to gather. 'Gather (ajlib) against them.'

extendedMeaning: Overwhelming greatness and majesty that inspires awe.
quranUsage: Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram - Owner of Majesty and Honor. Jalal is Allah's majestic aspect.
notes: Jalal (majesty) complements Jamal (beauty) in describing Allah.

quranUsage: Janaf (جنف) is inclination. 'Fearing inclination (janaf) to sin.'
'Its harvest (janaha) is near.' Jany is picking fruit.
notes: Paradise fruits are easy to pick.

quranUsage: Jud is generosity. Jawad is generous. Jayyid is excellent.
notes: The Prophet was the most generous of people.

quranUsage: Habasa means to confine. 'Detain (tahbisuna) them.'
Hajiz is barrier. 'Preventing (hajiz) them.'
Hatab (حطب) is firewood. 'Carrier of firewood (hatab).'
Hatta means to remove. 'Remove (hittah) from us.'
Hazir (حظير) is enclosure. 'Like uprooted trunks of palm trees.'
Hafara means to dig. Hafirah is pit.
Haffa means to surround. 'Surrounded (hafin) by angels.'
Huqub (حقب) is a long time. 'For ages (ahqaban).'
Hinth (حنث) is great sin. 'They persisted in the great sin (hinth).'
'When it reaches the throat (hanajir).' Hanjara is throat.
notes: At death, the soul rises to the throat.

quranUsage: Istawhadha means to gain control.
Mahshur is gathered.
Hawa means to gather. Hawaya is intestines.
Khabal (خبال) is corruption. 'They would increase you in corruption (khabal).'
Ukhdud (أخدود) is trench. 'Companions of the ukhdud (trench).'
Akhdan (أخدان) are secret friends. 'Not taking secret friends (akhdan).'
Khariba means to be ruined. 'They ruin (yukhribuna) their houses.'
Khardal (خردل) is mustard. 'A mustard seed (khardal).'
Yakhsifan means to patch. 'They patch (yakhsifan) over themselves.'
'Their necks would be submitting (khadi'in).' Khudu' is submission.
notes: Lowering oneself in submission to Allah.

quranUsage: Khamada means to die out. Khamidun are extinct.
Khamsah is hunger. Makhmasa is hunger.
Khannas (خناس) is the whisperer who withdraws.
Khuwar (خوار) is lowing. 'A calf body with a lowing (khuwar) sound.'
'When the sky brings visible smoke (dukhan).' Dukhan is smoke.
notes: Surah Ad-Dukhan mentions smoke as a sign.

quranUsage: Dam' (دمع) is tears. 'Overflowing with tears (dam').'

extendedMeaning: Long stretches of time, or fate/destiny. The passage of eras.
quranUsage: 'Has there come upon man a period (dahr) when he was nothing?' The dahr is time that passes.
notes: The Prophet forbade cursing 'dahr' as Allah controls time.

quranUsage: Dawlah (دولة) is circulation. 'Not circulating (dulatan) among the rich.'
'Even if a fly (dhubab) should steal from them.' Dhubab is fly.
notes: Idols cannot retrieve what a fly takes - showing their weakness.

quranUsage: Rajja means to shake. 'The earth is shaken (rujjat).'

extendedMeaning: Being deeply rooted and firmly established in knowledge.
quranUsage: 'Those firmly rooted (rasikhun) in knowledge.' Rusukh is being grounded.
notes: Scholars firmly rooted in knowledge understand the Quran properly.

quranUsage: Rass (رس) is a well. 'Companions of the Rass.'
'Fresh ripe dates (rutab) will fall upon you.' Rutab is ripe dates.
notes: Maryam was told to shake the palm for fresh dates.

extendedMeaning: Thunder and the trembling it causes. A sign of Allah's power.
quranUsage: Ar-Ra'd (The Thunder) is Surah 13. 'The thunder glorifies His praise.'
notes: Thunder is described as praising Allah.

quranUsage: Rufat (رفات) are particles. 'Bones and crumbled particles (rufatan).'
Rafath (رفث) is intimacy. 'No rafath (intimacy) during Hajj.'
Rifd (رفد) is support. 'Evil is the support (rifd).'

extendedMeaning: Sleeping, lying down, or being in a dormant state.
quranUsage: 'Who has raised us from our sleeping place (marqad)?' - said on resurrection.
notes: The grave is called marqad (sleeping place).

quranUsage: Arkasa means to turn back. 'Allah turned them back (arkasahum).'
Ramim (رميم) is decayed. 'Bones decayed (ramim).'
Rawdah (روضة) is garden. 'In a garden (rawdah).'
'The glass (zujajah) as if it were a brilliant star.' Zujaj is glass.
notes: The famous Light Verse describes a lamp in glass.

quranUsage: Zuhziha means to be removed. 'Removed (zuhziha) from Hell.'
Zalaq is slippery. 'Slippery (zalaqan) ground.'
Azlam (أزلام) are divining arrows.
Zumar (زمر) are groups. 'In groups (zumaran).'
notes: Surah 39 is Az-Zumar.

quranUsage: Zad (زاد) is provision. 'Take provisions (zad).'
Saba' (سبأ) is Sheba. Surah 34.
Sabighat are full. 'Full-length (sabighat) coats of armor.'
Suhuq (سحيق) is distant. 'A distant (sahiq) place.'
Sarmadan is perpetual. 'Night perpetual (sarmadan).'
Su'ida means to be happy. 'Those who are blessed (su'idu).'
Yasfiku means to shed. 'Sheds (yasfiku) blood.'
Saqim (سقيم) is ill. 'I am ill (saqim).'
'Those who are heedless (sahun) of their prayer.' Sahw is forgetfulness.
notes: Being negligent about prayer is condemned.

quranUsage: Shakhisa means to stare. 'Their eyes staring (shakhisah).'
Shati' (شاطئ) is bank. 'On the bank (shati') of the valley.'
'We made you into peoples (shu'ub) and tribes.' Sha'b is people.
notes: Diversity of peoples is for knowing each other.

quranUsage: Shughul (شغل) is occupation. 'In occupation (shughul).'
Shafa (شفا) is edge. 'On the edge (shafa) of a pit.'
'Each acts according to his manner (shakilah).' Shakl is form/shape.
notes: Everyone acts according to their nature/disposition.

quranUsage: 'For them therein is inhaling (shahiq).' Shahiq is gasping/inhaling.
notes: The people of Hell gasp for breath.

quranUsage: 'A roasted (hanidh) calf.' Shawy is roasting.
notes: Ibrahim's guests were served roasted calf.

quranUsage: Mushayyadah is fortified. 'Fortified (mushayyadah) towers.'
Asabi' (أصابع) are fingers. 'Their fingers (asabi'ahum) in their ears.'
Ṣadā (صدى) is echo. Related to sound returning.
Saghat means to incline. 'Their hearts inclined (saghat).'
Asfad (أصفاد) are chains. 'In chains (asfad).'
Sinwan (صنوان) are offshoots. 'Offshoots (sinwan) and single.'

extendedMeaning: Melting metal, smelting, and marriage relations.
quranUsage: 'It will melt (yusharu) what is in their bellies.' Sahr is melting.
notes: In-laws (ashar) are bonded like melted metals.

quranUsage: Adghaan (أضغان) are grudges. 'What is in your hearts of grudges (adghanakum).'
Idmum means to join. 'Join (udmum) to yourself.'
Tariy (طري) is fresh. 'Fresh (tariyyan) meat.'
Ta'ana means to criticize. 'Criticize (ta'anu) your religion.'
Yatmith means to touch. 'No human has touched (yatmithhunna) them.'
'Every animal with claws (zufur).' Zufr is nail/claw. Zafar is victory.
notes: Certain animals with claws were forbidden to Jews.

quranUsage: 'Abath (عبث) is play. 'We created you in play ('abathan)?'
'Freeing ('itq) a slave.' 'Itq is emancipation. 'Atiq is freed.
notes: Freeing slaves is highly meritorious in Islam.

quranUsage: 'Utul (عتل) is cruel. 'Cruel ('utul), moreover base-born.'
'Athara means to find. 'If it is found ('uthira) that they deserve.'
'Ijaf (عجاف) are lean. 'Seven lean ('ijaf) cows.'
Related to nakedness.
Ya'zubu means to be absent. 'Not absent (ya'zubu) from Him.'
'Adud (عضد) is support. 'I did not take them as support ('adudan).'
'Adda means to bite. 'Biting ('adda) his hands.'
Ta'duluhunna means to prevent. 'Do not prevent (ta'duluhunna) them.'
'Uttilat means disabled. 'The camels disabled ('uttilat).'
'The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah is that of the spider ('ankabut).' 'Ankabut is spider.
notes: The spider's web represents the weakness of false protectors.

quranUsage: 'Ihn (عهن) is wool. 'Like colored wool ('ihn).'
'A'ala means to have dependents. 'Fearing poverty ('aylah).'
'Ayiya means to be unable. 'We were not unable ('ayiyna).'
Yughithu means to help. Related to ghawth (help).
'If you fear treachery (khiyanah) from a people.' Ghadr is treachery.
notes: Breaking treaties is a form of treachery.

quranUsage: La gharwa means no wonder. 'No wonder (gharwa).'
Ghashiya/yughshi means to cover.
Ghulf (غلف) are covered. 'Our hearts are covered (ghulf).'
Ghuluww (غلو) is excess. 'Do not exceed (taghlu) in religion.'
'It will boil (taghli) in the bellies.' Ghalayan is boiling.
notes: Hell's drink boils in the stomachs.

quranUsage: Ghawwas is diver. 'Divers (ghawwasin).'
Ghawt (غوط) is depth.
Ghada means to decrease. 'The water subsided (ghida).'
'The freeing (fakk) of a slave.' Fakk is release.
notes: Freeing slaves is highly rewarded.

quranUsage: Iqtaḥama means to assault. ''Aqabah (عقبة) is steep path.'
Iqtadih means follow. 'Follow (iqtadih) their guidance.'
Qirṭās (قرطاس) is paper. 'A scripture on paper (qirṭās).'
Qisṭās (قسطاس) is scales. 'Weigh with the straight balance (qisṭās).'
'Its clusters (qutuf) hanging low.' Qatf is picking. Qutuf are clusters.
notes: Paradise fruit hangs low for easy picking.

quranUsage: Qalā is to roast. Related to cooking.
Muqni' (مقنع) is humble/raised. 'Heads raised (muqni'ī).' Qāni' is content.
Aqwāt (أقوات) are provisions. 'Its provisions (aqwātahā).'
Qā'idīn (قاعدين) are sitting. Related to sitting/staying behind.
Qayyaḍnā means We assigned. 'We assigned (qayyaḍnā) to them companions.'
Maqīl (مقيل) is resting place. 'Better in resting place (maqīlan).'
Kubkibū means thrown down. 'They will be thrown (kubkibū) into it.'
Kādih (كادح) is toiling. 'You are toiling (kādiḥun) toward your Lord.'
Kursī (كرسي) is throne/seat. 'His throne (kursiyyuhu) extends over the heavens.'
Kusālā (كسالى) are lazy. 'They come to prayer lazy (kusālā).'
Kalā'an means guardian. Related to protection.
Akmām (أكمام) are sheaths/spathes. 'From its sheaths (akmāmihā).'
Akmah (أكمه) is born blind. 'The blind (akmah) and the leper.'
Kahl (كهل) is middle-aged. 'In middle age (kahlan).'
Kāhin (كاهن) is soothsayer. 'Nor the word of a soothsayer (kāhin).'
Kayna is a defective form. Related to state of being.
Libad (لبدا) is crowded. 'Almost crowding (libadan) upon him.'
'Rivers of milk (laban) unchanged in taste.' Laban is milk.
notes: Paradise has rivers of pure, unchanging milk.

quranUsage: Aladd (ألد) is fierce. 'The fiercest (aladda) of opponents.'
Lughūb (لغوب) is fatigue. 'No fatigue (lughūb) touches us.'
Yaltaqiṭhu means to pick up. 'Some travelers will pick him up (yaltaqiṭhu).'
Lamḥ (لمح) is glance. 'Like a glance (lamḥ) of sight.'
Lamam (لمم) is minor sins. 'Except the small faults (lamam).'
Yalhath means to pant. 'He pants (yalhath).'
Yumḥaṣu means to purify. 'That Allah may purify (yumḥiṣa) the believers.'
Yamḥaq means to destroy. 'Allah destroys (yamḥaq) usury.'
'Allah has tested (imtahana) their hearts for taqwa.' Mihnah is ordeal/trial.
notes: Imtihan is examination/test.

quranUsage: Mawākhir (مواخر) are plowing ships. 'Ships plowing (mawākhir) through it.'
'This is salty (milh) and bitter.' Milh is salt.
notes: Two seas - fresh and salty - do not mix.

quranUsage: Imlāq (إملاق) is poverty. 'Out of fear of poverty (imlāq).'
Yanba'u means to gush. 'From which twelve springs gushed (inbajasa/yanba'u).'
An-Nahl (The Bee) is Surah 16. 'Your Lord inspired the bee.' Honey is healing.
notes: Bees receive divine inspiration (wahy) for their work.

quranUsage: Yunzafūna means intoxicated. 'They will not be intoxicated (yunzafūna).'
Nasī' (نسيء) is postponement. 'Postponement (nasī') is an increase in disbelief.'
Nāshiṭāt are those that draw out. 'Those that draw out (nāshiṭāt).'
Anṣitū means listen silently. 'Listen to it and be silent (anṣitū).'
Nu'ās (نعاس) is slumber. 'When He covered you with slumber (nu'āsan).'
Manfūsh (منفوش) is carded. 'Like carded (manfūsh) wool.'
Nākibūn means turning aside. 'From the path are turning aside (nākibūn).'
Nakasa means to recoil. 'He recoiled (nakasa) on his heels.'
Habā' (هباء) is scattered dust. 'Scattered dust (habā'an).'
Yuhra'ūna means hastening. 'His people hastening (yuhra'ūna) to him.'
Hashīm (هشيم) is crushed. 'Crushed (hashīman) dry.'
Haḍm (هضم) is oppression. 'He will not fear oppression (haḍman).'
Halumma means come. 'Come (halumma) to us.'
Muhaymin (مهيمن) is guardian. 'A guardian (muhayminan) over it.'
Inhāra means collapsed. 'So it collapsed (inhāra).'
'Then it withers (yahij).' Hayj is excitement. Hayyaj is one who stirs.
notes: Plants grow green then wither to yellow.

quranUsage: Yahīmūn means they wander. 'In every valley they wander (yahīmūn).'
Mawbiq (موبق) is place of destruction. 'Between them is a barrier (mawbiqan).'
Awjaftum means you spurred. 'You did not spur (awjaftum) any horse.'
Wadq (ودق) is rain. 'You see the rain (wadq) coming forth.'
Wasaq means gathered. 'And the night and what it gathers (wasaq).'
Wasīlah (وسيلة) is means. 'Seek means (wasīlah) to Him.'
Musawwamah (مسومة) is marked. 'Marked (musawwamatan) horses.'
Wāṣib (واصب) is perpetual. 'His is the religion perpetual (wāṣiban).'
Waṭar (وطر) is need. 'Zayd had fulfilled his need (waṭar).'
Abb (أب) is herbage. 'And fruits and abb (herbage).'
Abaqa means to flee. 'When he fled (abaqa) to the laden ship.'
notes: Refers to Prophet Yunus.

quranUsage: Athl (أثل) is tamarisk. 'Gardens of athl (tamarisk).'
Iddan (إدا) is monstrous. 'A monstrous (iddan) thing.'
Asin (آسن) is stagnant. 'Water not stagnant (asin).'
Alata means to diminish. 'We do not diminish (nalituhum).'
Amt (أمت) is crookedness. 'You see no amt (crookedness) in it.'
Anam (أنام) is creatures. 'He laid the earth for the anam (creatures).'
Ada/ya'udu means to burden. 'It does not burden (ya'uduhu) Him.'
Ayyim (أيم) is unmarried. 'Marry the unmarried (ayama) among you.'
Bi'r (بئر) is well. 'A well (bi'r) disabled.'
Abtar (أبتر) is cut off. 'Your enemy is the one cut off (abtar).'
Battaka means to cut. 'They will cut (yubattikanna) the ears of cattle.'
Inbajasa means to gush. 'Twelve springs gushed (inbajasat) forth.'
Bahatha means to search. 'A crow searching (yabhath) in the ground.'

extendedMeaning: Full moon, or the Battle of Badr.
quranUsage: Badr (بدر) is the battle site. 'At Badr when you were few.'
Basiqat (باسقات) are tall. 'Tall (basiqat) palm trees.'
Tabassama means to smile. 'He smiled (tabassama) laughing.'
Basal (بصل) is onion. 'Its herbs and onions (basal).'
Bata'a means to be slow. 'Among you is one who is slow (yubatti').'
'Horses, mules (bighal), and donkeys.' Baghl is mule.
notes: Mules are mentioned among riding animals.

quranUsage: Buq'ah (بقعة) is spot. 'In the blessed buq'ah (spot).'
Baql (بقل) is herbs. 'Its herbs (baql) and cucumbers.'
Bala'a means to swallow. 'O earth, swallow (ibla'i) your water.'
Mubahalah is mutual cursing. 'Let us invoke (nabtahil) and invoke Allah's curse.'
Bayda means to destroy. 'May it destroy (tubidu) them.'
Taraqiy (تراقي) are collarbones. 'When it reaches the collarbones (taraqiy).'
Ta'san (تعسا) is destruction. 'Destruction (ta'san) for them.'
Tafath (تفث) is dirt. 'Let them end their tafath (unkemptness).'
Atqana means to perfect. 'The making of Allah who perfected (atqana).'
Talla means to throw down. 'He threw (tallahu) him on his forehead.'
'By the fig (tin) and the olive.' At-Tin is Surah 95.
notes: The fig is mentioned alongside the olive in a divine oath.

quranUsage: Taha means to wander. 'They will wander (yatihun) in the land.'
Thabbata means to hold back. 'Allah held them back (thabbatahum).'
Related to being firm.
Thajjaj (ثجاج) is pouring. 'Water pouring (thajjajan) abundantly.'
Thariiba means no blame. 'No blame (tathrib) on you today.'
Thara (ثرى) is moist earth. 'What is in the moist earth (thara).'
Thayyib (ثيب) is previously married. 'Previously married (thayyibat) and virgins.'
Jibt (جبت) is idol. 'They believe in jibt (idols).'
Related to being cowardly.

extendedMeaning: Forehead - the noble part placed in prostration.
quranUsage: 'Their foreheads (jibah), sides, and backs will be branded.' Jabhah is forehead.
notes: The forehead touches the ground in sujud.

quranUsage: Ijtuthat means uprooted. 'Its root uprooted (ijtuthat).'
Jadhwah (جذوة) is firebrand. 'A firebrand (jadhwah) to warm.'
Jarra means to drag. Related to dragging.
Yatajarra'u means to gulp. 'He gulps (yatajarra'uhu) it.'
Juruf (جرف) is edge. 'On the edge (juruf) of a crumbling bank.'
Tajassasu means to spy. 'Do not spy (tajassasu).'
Jufa' (جفاء) is foam. 'The foam (jufa') goes away.'
'Large bowls (jifan) like reservoirs.' Jafnah is large bowl.
notes: Sulayman had large bowls for feeding many people.

quranUsage: Tatajafa means to leave. 'Their sides leave (tatajafa) beds.'
'Make room in assemblies (majalis).' Julus is sitting. Majlis is assembly.
notes: Make room for others in gatherings.

quranUsage: Jamaha means to rush. 'They rush (yajmahun) headlong.'
'You see the mountains thinking them solid (jamidah).' Jumud is solidity.
notes: Mountains appear solid but will move on Judgment Day.

quranUsage: Jamm (جم) is abundant. 'You love wealth with abundant (jamman) love.'
Jasu means to traverse. 'They traversed (jasu) through the land.'
Jawf (جوف) is interior. 'In his interior (jawf) two hearts.'
'Birds in the atmosphere (jaww) of the sky.' Jaww is atmosphere.
notes: Birds fly in the atmosphere by Allah's permission.

quranUsage: Jid (جيد) is neck. 'Around her jid (neck) a rope.'
'The sky with its tight weaving (hubuk).' Hubuk is tight weaving.
notes: The sky is described as tightly woven/constructed.

quranUsage: Hatm is decree. 'It is a decree (hatman) decided.'
Haththa means to urge.
'From every elevation (hadab).' Hadab is elevation/slope.
notes: People will come from every hill and slope.

quranUsage: Hard (حرد) is determination. 'They went early with hard (determination).'
Harasa means to guard. Haras are guards.
'Do not move (tuharrik) your tongue hastily.' Harakah is movement.
notes: The Prophet was told not to rush in reciting revelation.

quranUsage: Hariyy (حري) is worthy.
Husum (حسوم) is continuous. 'Seven nights, continuous (husum).'
Hashasa means to become clear. 'Now the truth has become clear (hashasa).'
Hussila means to be brought out. 'What is in the chests is brought out (hussila).'
Hafadah (حفدة) are grandchildren. 'Sons and grandchildren (hafadah).'
Ahqaf (أحقاف) are sand dunes. Surah 46.
Hanidh (حنيذ) is roasted. 'A roasted (hanidh) calf.'
Hanak is palate. Related to the mouth.
notes: Part of the intricate design of the mouth.

quranUsage: Hanan (حنان) is tenderness. 'Compassion (hananan) from Us.'
Hub (حوب) is sin. 'It is ever a great sin (huban).'
Tahawwaza means to take aside. 'Or taking aside (mutahayyizan).'
Hada means to turn aside. 'Turning aside (yahid).'
'Confused (hayran) in the earth.' Hayrah is confusion. Ha'ir is confused.
notes: Without guidance, people wander confused.

quranUsage: Hayf (حيف) is injustice. 'Fearing injustice (yahifa).'
Khab' is hidden. 'Hidden (khabaya) treasure.'
'I saw myself carrying bread (khubz).' Khubz is bread.
notes: The king's baker dreamed of carrying bread.

quranUsage: Takhabatahu means to confuse. 'Satan confuses (yatakhabbatuhu) him.'
Khabat means to subside. 'Whenever it subsides (khabat).'
Khattar is treacherous.
Khurtum (خرطوم) is nose. 'We will brand him on the nose (khurtum).'
'As if they were pieces of wood (khushub).' Khashab is wood.
notes: Hypocrites are likened to propped-up pieces of wood.

quranUsage: Khud means bent. 'Among thornless lote trees (makhdhud).'
Khatt (خط) is writing. 'You could not write (takhutt) it.'
Ikhla' means to remove. 'Remove (ikhla') your sandals.'
Khamt (خمط) is bitter. 'Bitter fruit (ukul khamt).'
Munkhaniqa is strangled. 'The strangled (munkhaniqah).'
Khiyam (خيام) are tents. 'In tents (khiyam).'
Muddaththir (مدثر) is one wrapped. Surah 74.
Dahaha means to spread. 'The earth He spread (dahaha).'
Darahim are dirhams. 'A few dirhams (darahim).'
Dusur (دسر) are planks. 'Planks (alwah) and dusur (nails).'
Dassa means to bury. 'He who corrupts (dassaha) it.'
Dassa means to corrupt.
Dif' (دفء) is warmth. 'In them is warmth (dif').'
Dafiq (دافق) is gushing. 'Gushing (dafiq) water.'
Duluk (دلوك) is decline. 'From the decline (duluk) of the sun.'
Damdama means to destroy. 'Their Lord destroyed (damdama) them.'
Yadmaghu means to crush. 'To crush (fayadmaghuhu) it.'
Dinar (دينار) is gold coin.
Dihaq (دهاق) is overflowing. 'A cup overflowing (dihaq).'
Mudhammatani are dark green. 'Dark green (mudhammatani).'
Dahiya is calamity. 'The great calamity (dahiya).'
Madhum is blamed. 'Blameworthy (madhuman).'
Muthadhdhidin are wavering. 'Wavering (muthadhdhidin) between.'
Adkhara means to store. 'What you stored (taddakhirun).'
Mudh'inun are submissive. 'Submissive (mudh'inin).'
Dhakkaha means to slaughter. 'Except what you slaughter (dhakkaytum).'
'Every nursing mother will forget (tadhhal).' Dhuhul is distraction.
notes: The terror of Judgment Day will make mothers forget their infants.

quranUsage: Tadhudan means to drive away. 'Two women driving (tadhudani).'
Adha'u means to spread. 'They spread (adha'u) it.'
'Their trade did not profit (rabihat) them.' Ribh is profit.
notes: Those who trade guidance for misguidance lose their profit.

quranUsage: Yarta'u means to enjoy. 'Play and enjoy (yarta').'
Ratq is joined. 'They were joined (ratqan).'
Rahiq (رحيق) is nectar. 'Sealed nectar (rahiq makhtum).'
Rukhawah is looseness. Rakhi is loose/relaxed.
notes: After hardship comes ease and relaxation.

quranUsage: Rid' (ردء) is helper. 'As a helper (rid'an).'
Radm (ردم) is barrier. 'Shall I make a barrier (radm)?'
'As if they were a compact structure (marsus).' Rasas is lead.
notes: Believers fighting in rows are like a solid, leaded structure.

quranUsage: Raghama means to humble. 'Wide (muragham).'
Rafarif (رفارف) are cushions. 'Green cushions (rafarif).'
'Their skins shiver (taqsha'irru).' Riqq is thinness. Riqqa is tenderness.
notes: Believers' hearts are tender to Allah's words.

quranUsage: Rawakid are still. 'Ships still (rawakid).'
Rikz (ركز) is faint sound. 'Any faint sound (rikzan).'
Rumh is spear. Rimah is spears.
notes: Spears were common weapons in early Islamic battles.

quranUsage: Ramad (رماد) is ashes. 'Like ashes (ramad).'
Ramz (رمز) is signal. 'Except by signal (ramzan).'
Ramadan (رمضان) is the fasting month.
Rahw (رهو) is calm. 'Leave the sea calm (rahwan).'
Raw' (روع) is fear. 'When fear (raw') left Ibrahim.'
Rish (ريش) is feathers. 'Adornment (rishan).'
Ri' (ريع) is elevated place. 'On every elevated place (ri').'
Rana means to cover. 'Covered (rana) their hearts.'
Zabaniyah (زبانية) are guards of Hell.

extendedMeaning: Crawling, advancing slowly like an army.
quranUsage: 'When you meet those who disbelieve advancing (zahfan).' Zahf is crawling advance.
notes: Armies advance slowly like crawling.

quranUsage: Zarabiy (زرابي) are carpets. 'Rich carpets (zarabiy).'

extendedMeaning: Blue color, particularly pale blue of blind eyes.
quranUsage: 'We will gather the criminals that Day blue (zurqa)' - blind/terrified.
notes: Zurq describes the terrified appearance of criminals.

quranUsage: Tazri means to despise. 'You despise (tazri) them.'
Yaziffun means to hasten. 'Hastening (yaziffun).'
Muzzammil (مزمل) is one wrapped. Surah 73.
Zamharir (زمهرير) is extreme cold.
Zanim (زنيم) is base-born. 'A base-born (zanim).'
'They sold him for a small price, showing no interest (zahidin).' Zuhd is asceticism.
notes: Zuhd is not wanting what you don't have.

quranUsage: Zahrah (زهرة) is splendor. 'The splendor (zahrata) of the world.'
Saja means to become still. 'When the night covers (saja).'
Sahil (ساحل) is coast. Related to coastal areas.
Suda (سدى) is neglected. 'Left neglected (sudan).'
Sard (سرد) is linked. 'Link (qaddir) the rings.'
Suradiq (سرادق) is canopy. 'Its canopy (suradiquha) surrounds.'
'How it was spread out (sutihat).' Sath is surface.
notes: The earth was spread out as a surface.

quranUsage: Yastuna means to assault. 'They almost assault (yastuna).'
Masghaba (مسغبة) is hunger. 'A day of hunger (masghaba).'
Nasfa' means to seize. 'We will seize (lanasfa'an) the forelock.'
Maskub is poured. 'Water poured (maskub).'
Sakata means to be silent. 'When anger subsided (sakata).'
Yaslubu means to snatch. 'If a fly snatches (yaslubu).'
Salaqukum means to assault. 'With sharp tongues (salaqukum).'
Samidun are haughty. 'Haughty (samidun).'
Samk (سمك) is structure. 'Its structure (samkaha).'
Musannadah are propped. 'Propped (musannadah) pieces of wood.'
Sanam (سنام) is hump. Related to high status.
'A thousand years (sanah).' Sanah is year. Sanawat is years.
notes: Nuh called his people for 950 years.

quranUsage: Sahirah (ساهرة) is wide awake. 'On an open plain (sahirah).'
'We will ease (sayassiru) him toward ease.' Sahl is easy. Taysir is facilitation.
notes: Allah makes things easy for the righteous.

quranUsage: Sahm (سهم) is lot. Related to drawing lots.
Siha means to travel. 'Travel (sihu) in the land.'
Sawt (سوط) is whip. 'Poured upon them a whip (sawta) of punishment.'
Sa'ibah (سائبة) is she-camel let loose.
'The journey (rihlah) of winter (shita') and summer.' Shita' is winter.
notes: Quraysh's winter journey was to Yemen.

quranUsage: Shahm (شحم) is fat. 'Their fat (shuhumahuma).'
Sharrida means to disperse. 'Disperse (sharrid) with them.'
Shirdhimah (شرذمة) is small group.
Ashrat (أشراط) are signs. 'Its signs (ashratuha) have come.'
Ishta'ala means to kindle. 'My head has kindled (ishta'ala) with gray.'
Shaghafa means to infatuate. 'He has infatuated (shaghafaha) her.'
'Two lips (shafatayn)' - among Allah's blessings. Shafah is lip.
notes: Lips are mentioned as blessings enabling speech.

quranUsage: Mutashakisun are quarrelsome. 'Quarrelsome (mutashakisun) partners.'
Tushmit means to make gloat. 'Do not let enemies gloat (tushmit).'
Shamikh is lofty. 'Lofty (shamikhat) mountains.'
Ishma'azzat means to shrink. 'Their hearts shrink (ishma'azzat).'
Shawb (شوب) is mixture. 'A mixture (shawban) of boiling water.'
Shuwaz (شواظ) is flame. 'A flame (shuwaz) of fire.'
'No food except thorny plants (dari').' Shawk is thorn.
notes: The food of Hell includes thorny plants.

quranUsage: Sakhkhah (صاخة) is deafening blast. 'The deafening blast (sakhkhah).'
Sar'a is felled. 'As if felled (munqa'ir) palm trunks.'
Tusa'ir means to turn. 'Do not turn (tusa'ir) your cheek.'
Safsaf (صفصف) is level. 'A level plain (safsafan).'
Safinat (صافنات) are standing horses.
Sakkat means to strike. 'She struck (sakkat) her face.'
Saldan (صلدا) is smooth rock. 'Smooth rock (saldan).'
Samt is silence. Samit is silent.
notes: Silence can be wisdom or can be sinful when truth must be spoken.

extendedMeaning: The one to whom all turn in need, yet needs nothing from anyone.
quranUsage: As-Samad appears in Surah Al-Ikhlas - Allah is As-Samad, the Eternal Refuge.
notes: Samad implies Allah is sought by all but needs none.

quranUsage: Sawami' (صوامع) are monasteries.
Suwa' (صواع) is cup. 'The king's cup (suwa').'
'Mountains will be like carded wool (suf).' Suf is wool. Sufi relates to wool-wearers.
notes: Mountains becoming like wool describes their destruction.

quranUsage: Sayasi (صياصي) are fortresses. 'From their fortresses (sayasihim).'
'The journey of winter and summer (sayf).' Sayf is summer.
notes: Quraysh's summer journey was to Syria.

quranUsage: Da'n (ضأن) is sheep. 'Of the sheep (da'n) two.'
Dabh (ضبح) is panting. 'Panting (dabhan).'
Diddan (ضدا) is opponent. 'Be opponents (diddan).'
'We sent upon them the flood, locusts, lice, frogs (dafadi').' Difda' is frog.
notes: Frogs were among the plagues sent to Pharaoh.

quranUsage: Damir (ضامر) is lean. 'On every lean (damir) camel.'
Dank (ضنك) is straitened. 'A straitened (dankan) life.'
Danin (ضنين) is stingy. 'Not stingy (danin).'
Dahiya is barren.
Dayr (ضير) is harm. 'No harm (dayr) upon us.'
Diza (ضيزى) is unjust. 'An unjust (diza) division.'
Tahaha means to spread. 'The earth He spread (tahaha).'
'Cast (itrahuh) Yusuf into the well.' Tarh is throwing/casting.
notes: Yusuf's brothers cast him into the well.

extendedMeaning: Giving less than due, cheating in measure.
quranUsage: 'Woe to those who give less (mutaffifin).' Tatfif is cheating in measure.
notes: Surah Al-Mutaffifin condemns cheating merchants.

quranUsage: Talh (طلح) is banana. 'And banana trees (talh) layered.'
Tall (طل) is fine rain. 'Fine rain (tall).'
Tammah (طامة) is overwhelming. 'The great overwhelming (tammah).'
Tawd (طود) is mountain. 'Like a mountain (tawd).'
Za'n (ظعن) is traveling. 'On the day of your travel (za'nikum).'
Ya'ba'u means to care. 'What would my Lord care (ya'ba'u)?'
'Abqariy (عبقري) are rich carpets.
'Adas (عدس) is lentils. 'Its lentils ('adas).'
'Urjun (عرجون) is old palm stalk. 'Like an old palm stalk ('urjun).'
'Arim (عرم) is dam. 'The flood of the dam ('arim).'
'Izin are groups. 'In separate groups ('izin).'
'As'asa means to darken. 'When the night darkens ('as'as).'
'Rivers of honey ('asal) purified.' 'In it is healing for people.'
notes: Honey is described as having healing properties.

quranUsage: 'Idin is portions. 'Into portions ('idin).'
'Atafa means to turn. 'Turning ('atafa) his side.'
'Afar is dust. Related to dust.
'From every deep (amiq) mountain pass.' 'Umq is depth. 'Amiq is deep.
notes: Pilgrims come from every deep valley.

quranUsage: 'Anat means to submit. 'Faces will submit ('anat).'
Mu'awwiqin are hinderers. 'Those who hinder (mu'awwiqin).'
Ta'ulu means to be unjust. 'Closer to not being unjust (ta'ulu).'
'Ayb is defect. 'I wanted to defect ('a'ibaha) it.'
Taghabun (تغابن) is mutual loss/deception. Surah 64.
Ghadaqan (غدقا) is abundant. 'Abundant (ghadaqan) water.'
'Like her who unravels her spinning (ghazl).' Ghazl is spinning.
notes: Breaking oaths is like unraveling spun thread.

quranUsage: Ghazw is raid. 'Those who raid (ghuzzan).'
Ghasb is seizing. 'Seizes (ya'khudhu) by force.'
Ghussah (غصة) is choking. 'Food that chokes (ghussah).'
Aghtas means to darken. 'Its night (aghtasha).'
'She closed (ghallaqat) the doors.' Mughallaq is locked/closed.
notes: In Yusuf's story, she locked the doors attempting seduction.

quranUsage: Yataghamazun means to wink. 'They wink (yataghamazun).'
Tughmidu means to overlook. 'Unless you overlook (tughmidu).'
Ghawl (غول) is headache/intoxication. 'No ghawl (ill effect).'
Tafta'u means to cease. 'You will not cease (tafta'u).'
Fataq is split. 'We split (fataqnahuma) them.'
Fajwah (فجوة) is open space. 'In an open space (fajwah).'
Farth (فرث) is excrement. 'Between excrement (farth) and blood.'
'To Pharaoh (Fir'awn) and his chiefs.' Fir'awn is Pharaoh. Far' is branch.
notes: Pharaoh is the archetype of tyranny in the Quran.

quranUsage: Farihin are proud. 'Skillful (farihin).'
'We bring you the truth and the best explanation (tafsir).' Tafsir is explanation.
notes: Tafsir is the science of Quranic interpretation.

quranUsage: Afsahu means clearer. 'He is clearer (afsahu) in speech.'
Infisam is breaking. 'No break (infisam).'
Tafdhahuni means to disgrace. 'Do not disgrace (tafdhahuni) me.'
Afda means to turn. 'They turn away (afdaw).'
Fazz (فظ) is harsh. 'If you were harsh (fazzan).'
Faqi' (فاقع) is bright. 'Bright (faqi') yellow.'
Fulan (فلان) is so and so. 'I had not taken so and so (fulanan).'
Tufannidun means to accuse. 'You accuse me (tufannidun).'
Afnan (أفنان) are branches. 'With spreading branches (afnan).'

extendedMeaning: Perishing, ceasing to exist, and annihilation.
quranUsage: 'Everything upon it will perish (fan).' Fana' is annihilation.
notes: All creation is subject to fana' - only Allah is eternal.

quranUsage: 'We gave Sulayman understanding (fahhamna).' Fahm is understanding.
notes: Sulayman was given special understanding of a case.

quranUsage: Ufawwidu means to entrust. 'I entrust (ufawwidu) my affair.'
Fum (فوم) is garlic. 'Its garlic (fumaha).'
Fil (فيل) is elephant. Surah Al-Fil. 'Companions of the elephant (fil).'
'Evil (qubh) is the abode of the arrogant.' Qabih is ugly/bad.
notes: Qubh is the opposite of husn (beauty/goodness).

quranUsage: Qithā' (قثاء) is cucumber. 'Its cucumbers (qithā'ihā).'
Qadaḥ (قدح) is cup. Qādihāt: strike fire. 'Those that strike sparks (qādihāt).'
Quraysh (قريش) is Quraysh. Surah Quraysh. 'For the accustomed security of Quraysh.'
Qaswarah (قسورة) is lion/hunters. 'Fleeing from a lion (qaswarah).'
Qissīsīn (قسيسين) are priests. 'Priests (qissīsīna) and monks.'
Taqsha'irru means to shudder. 'Their skins shudder (taqsha'irru).'
Qāṣif (قاصف) is breaking. 'A breaking (qāṣifan) wind.'
Qaṣamnā means We destroyed. 'How many We destroyed (qaṣamnā).'
Qaḍb (قضب) is fodder. 'And fodder (qaḍban).'
Inqaḍḍa means to collapse. 'About to collapse (yanqaḍḍ).'
Taquṭṭu means to drop. Related to cutting off.
Qiṭmīr (قطمير) is date-stone membrane. 'Not even a membrane (qiṭmīran).'
'To the bottom (qa'r) of the pit.' Qa'r is bottom.
notes: Hell has deep bottoms.

quranUsage: 'Or are there locks (aqfal) upon their hearts?' Qufl is lock.
notes: Hearts can be locked from understanding.

primaryMeaning: To pull something out by its roots, as a tree or a tooth is uprooted. The form aqlaʿa means to stop or give something up — as if pulling oneself away from it.
quranUsage: Occurs once, at 11:44, at the end of the Flood: 'O sky, withhold (aqliʿī)' — the sky is commanded to stop its rain.
Muqmaḥūn means raised heads. 'Heads raised (muqmaḥūn).'
Qamṭarīr (قمطرير) is distressful. 'A distressful (qamṭarīran) day.'
Maqāmi' (مقامع) are hammers. 'Hammers (maqāmi') of iron.'
'We sent upon them lice (qummal).' Qummal is lice.
notes: Lice were among Pharaoh's plagues.

quranUsage: Qinwān (قنوان) are date-stalks. 'Clusters (qinwān) of dates.'
Aqnā means He enriched. 'He enriched (aqnā) and gave property.'
Qiṭmīr (قطمير) is shell. Related to thin covering.
Qawsayn (قوسين) is two bows. 'Two bow-lengths (qawsayn).'
Kabad (كبد) is hardship. 'In hardship (kabad).'
Kubkibū means thrown down. 'They will be thrown (kubkibū) into it.'
Kathīb (كثيب) is sand dune. 'A heap (kathīban) poured.'
Kadar is murkiness. Kadira is to be turbid.
notes: The opposite of clarity and purity.

quranUsage: Akdā means gave little. 'And gave little (akdā).'
Takhshaw kasādahā means fearing stagnation. 'You fear will stagnate (kasādahā).'
Kushiṭat means stripped. 'When the sky is stripped (kushiṭat).'
Kufuwan (كفوا) is equivalent. 'None equivalent (kufuwan) to Him.'
Kifāt (كفات) is container. 'A container (kifātan).'
Kala' (كلأ) is herbage. 'And herbage (kala').'
Kāliḥūn (كالحون) are frowning. 'They will be frowning (kāliḥūn).'
Kanūd (كنود) is ungrateful. 'Man is ungrateful (kanūd).'
Kunnas (كنس) are retreating. 'The retreating (kunnas) stars.'
Tukwā means to brand. 'Their foreheads will be branded (tukwā).'
Ilḥāf (إلحاف) is persistence. 'They do not ask with persistence (ilḥāfan).'
Laḥn (لحن) is tone. 'You will know them by their tone (laḥn).'
Liḥyah (لحية) is beard. 'Do not pull my beard (liḥyatī).'
Lāzib (لازب) is sticky. 'From sticky (lāzib) clay.'
Laẓā (لظى) is blazing fire. 'It is the Flame (laẓā).'
Talfaḥu means to burn. 'The Fire will burn (talfaḥu) their faces.'
'He does not utter (yalfizu) any word.' Lafz is utterance.
notes: Every word we utter is recorded by angels.

quranUsage: Alqāb (ألقاب) are nicknames. 'Do not call by nicknames (alqāb).'
Lawāqiḥ (لواقح) are fertilizing. 'Winds fertilizing (lawāqiḥ).'
Luqmān (لقمان) is Luqman. Surah Luqman.
Alhamahā means He inspired it. 'He inspired it (alhamahā).'
Lūṭ (لوط) is Lot. Story of Prophet Lot.
Yatalawwadhūna means slinking away. 'Slinking away (yatalawwadhūna).'
Layta (ليت) is would that. 'Would that (layta) I had!'
Majūs (مجوس) are Magians. 'And the Magians (majūs).'
Maḥl (محل) is scheming. 'Severe in scheming (maḥl).'
Makhāḍ (مخاض) is labor. 'The labor pains (makhāḍ) drove her.'
Marwah (مروة) is Marwah. 'Ṣafā and Marwah.'
'We will set up the scales (mawazin) of justice.' Mizan is scale/balance.
notes: Deeds will be weighed on precise scales.

quranUsage: Masakhnāhum means We transformed. 'We transformed (masakhnāhum) them.'
Masad (مسد) is rope. Surah Al-Masad. 'A rope (masad) of palm fiber.'
Imsaḥū means wipe. 'Wipe (imsaḥū) your heads.'
Amshāj (أمشاج) is mixed. 'A drop mixed (amshāj).'
Yatamaṭṭā means to stretch. 'Then he went to his family strutting (yatamaṭṭā).'
'And of the goats (ma'z), two.' Ma'z is goat.
notes: Goats are mentioned among the eight pairs of livestock.

quranUsage: Am'ā' (أمعاء) are intestines. 'Cuts up their intestines (am'ā'ahum).'
Mukā'an (مكاء) is whistling. 'Whistling (mukā'an) and clapping.'
Namīru means we get provisions. 'We get provisions (namīru).'
Tanābazū means call names. 'Do not call names (tanābazū).'
Yastanbiṭūna means to extract. 'Those who extract (yastanbiṭūnahu) it.'
Nataqnā means We raised. 'We raised (nataqnā) the mountain.'
Najdayn (نجدين) are two ways. 'The two ways (najdayn).'
'The polytheists are impure (najas).' Najas is impurity. Najis is impure.
notes: Spiritual impurity of shirk is worse than physical impurity.

quranUsage: 'Some fulfilled their vow (nahb).' Nahib is sobbing. Nahb is vow fulfilled.
notes: Some believers fulfilled their pledge through martyrdom.

quranUsage: 'Pray and sacrifice (wanhar).' Nahr is sacrificing camels.
notes: Camels are sacrificed by cutting the throat area.

quranUsage: Nākhirah (ناخرة) is decayed. 'Decayed (nākhirah) bones.'
Nasr (نسر) is Nasr (idol). 'And Yaghūth and Ya'ūq and Nasr.'
Naḍijat means is roasted. 'Their skins are roasted (naḍijat).'
Naḍḍākhatān are gushing. 'Two gushing (naḍḍākhatān) springs.'
Naṭīḥah (نطيحة) is gored. 'That gored (naṭīḥah).'
'Like one who calls (yan'iqu) to that which hears nothing.' Na'iq is one who calls.
notes: Calling disbelievers is like calling animals that don't understand.

quranUsage: Na'layka (نعليك) is your sandals. 'Remove your sandals (na'layk).'
Yunghiḍūna means they shake. 'They shake (yunghiḍūna) their heads.'
Naffāthāt (نفاثات) are those who blow. 'Those who blow (naffāthāt) on knots.'
Nafḥah (نفحة) is breath. 'If a breath (nafḥatun) touches them.'
Yunfaw means banished. 'Or be banished (yunfaw).'
Naq' (نقع) is stirring up dust. 'Stirring up (naq'an) thereby dust.'
Nakidan (نكدا) is barren. 'It comes forth barren (nakidan).'
Namāriq (نمارق) are cushions. 'Cushions (namāriq) lined up.'
Nammām (نمام) is slanderer. 'A spreader of slander (nammām).'
Minhāj (منهاج) is path. 'A law and a path (minhājan).'
Tanū'u means to burden. 'Its keys would burden (tanū'u).'
Tanāwush (تناوش) is seizing. 'How can they seize (tanāwush) from afar?'
Manāṣ (مناص) is escape. 'No time for escape (manāṣ).'
Nūn (نون) is fish/letter. Surah Nūn. 'Companion of the fish (nūn).'
Niyyah is intention. The Prophet said: 'Actions are by intentions.'
notes: Every act of worship requires proper intention (niyyah).

quranUsage: Hā' is here/take. Related to presenting.

primaryMeaning: to stay awake, pray at night
quranUsage: Tahajjud (تهجد) is night prayer. 'Pray tahajjud (tahajjad).'
Hāji'ūn (هاجعون) are sleeping. Related to night rest.
Yahaddu means to collapse. 'About to collapse (yahaddu).'
'Destroyed (huddimat) would have been monasteries.' Hadm is demolition.
notes: Without Allah's protection, places of worship would be destroyed.

quranUsage: 'He inspected the birds and said: Why do I not see the hoopoe (hudhud)?' Hudhud is hoopoe.
notes: The hoopoe brought Sulayman news of the Queen of Sheba.

quranUsage: Harab (هرب) is fleeing. Related to escape.
Hazl (هزل) is jest. 'It is not a jest (hazl).'
Ahushsha means to beat down. 'I beat down (ahushsha) leaves.'
'Man was created anxious (halu'an).' Hala' is anxiety.
notes: Humans are naturally anxious except those who pray.

quranUsage: Hāmidah (هامدة) is lifeless. 'You see the earth lifeless (hāmidatan).'
Munhamir (منهمر) is pouring. 'Water pouring (munhamir).'
'You will hear only whispers (hams).' Hams is whisper.
notes: On Judgment Day, voices will be hushed before Allah.

quranUsage: Hayta means come. 'Come (hayta) to you.'
Mahīl (مهيل) is poured. 'A heap poured (mahīlan).'
Wu'idat means buried. 'When the girl buried alive (wu'idat) is asked.'
Maw'il (موئل) is refuge. 'No refuge (maw'ilan).'
Awbār (أوبار) is camel hair. 'From their wool and fur (awbārihā).'
Watīn (وتين) is life-artery. 'Cut from him the artery (watīn).'

extendedMeaning: Being necessary, obligatory, and falling due.
quranUsage: 'When their sides fall (wajabat).' Wajib is obligatory.
notes: Wajib in fiqh means religiously obligatory.

quranUsage: 'Wild beasts (wuhush) are gathered.' Wahsh is wild beast. Wahshah is loneliness.
notes: Wild animals will be gathered on Judgment Day.

quranUsage: Sinah (سنة) is drowsiness. 'Neither drowsiness (sinah) nor sleep.'
Wāshiyah (واشية) is embroidered. Related to decoration.
Mawḍūnah (موضونة) is inlaid. 'Inlaid (mawḍūnah) couches.'
Mawāṭin (مواطن) are places. 'In many places (mawāṭin).'
Wafd (وفد) is delegation. 'As a delegation (wafdan).'
'Reward most abundant (awfar).' Wafir is abundant.
notes: Allah's rewards are always abundant.

quranUsage: Yūfiḍūna means they hasten. 'They hasten (yūfiḍūna).'
Ghāsiq (غاسق) waqab is night when it settles. 'When it becomes dark (waqab).'
Mawqūdhah (موقوذة) is beaten to death. 'That beaten to death (mawqūdhah).'
Tawkīd (توكيد) is emphasis. Related to affirming.
Wakaz means to strike. 'He struck (wakazahu) him.'
Taniyā means to weaken. 'Do not weaken (taniyā).'
Wahhāj (وهاج) is blazing. 'A blazing (wahhājan) lamp.'
Wāhiyah (واهية) is weak/torn. 'Like a torn (wāhiyah) tent.'
'You would think them awake (ayqaz).' Yaqazah is wakefulness.
notes: The People of the Cave appeared awake while sleeping.

quranUsage: 'Look at its fruit when it ripens (yani').' Yan' is ripening.
notes: Fruit ripening is a sign of Allah's power.
